CHAIRMAN’S MESSAGE
ADITYA BIRLA LIFESTYLE BRANDS LIMITED INTEGRATED ANNUAL REPORT FY 2025-26In a global landscape defined by volatility, geopolitical 
tension, and accelerating technological change, FY26 has 
been a milestone year for the Group. Our large manufacturing 
businesses have consolidated their leadership positions, our 
newer ventures are scaling with conviction, and our legacy 
consumer businesses are being reshaped for a new era of 
growth. Across this diverse portfolio, one force continues to 
anchor our progress— trust.
Trust is often viewed as an intangible asset. In reality, 
it is one of the most consequential forms of capital an 
institution can possess. In periods of uncertainty, markets 
can turn volatile and competitive advantages can erode. 
Trust, however, compounds. It enables organisations to make 
long-term investments when others hesitate, to navigate 
disruption with credibility, and to emerge stronger from 
periods of change.
For a group such as ours, trust extends far beyond the 
relationship between a company and its customers. It is 
reflected in the confidence of shareholders who support 
long-term value creation, the commitment of employees 
who choose to build their careers with us, the faith of 
partners and suppliers who invest alongside us, and the 
confidence of communities and governments that see us as a 
responsible participant in economic progress. Each of these 
constituencies grants an institution something invaluable: the 
licence to grow.
This is particularly relevant at a time when businesses 
are being asked to do more than deliver financial 
performance. They are expected to navigate technological disruption, manage increasingly complex supply chains, 
create meaningful employment, steward natural resources 
responsibly and contribute to social progress. Meeting these 
expectations requires more than scale or strategy. It requires 
credibility built over years and, in many cases, decades.
The strength of our portfolio today reflects the cumulative 
effect of that credibility. It has allowed us to invest through 
cycles, pursue transformation with confidence and attract 
talent, capital, and partnerships that strengthen our 
competitive position. 
Global Economy in 2025
The global economy maintained its trajectory through 2025 
despite elevated tariffs, policy uncertainty, and geopolitical 
tensions. The impact of tariff measures was less severe 
than projections had suggested, and growth across major 
economies remained broadly stable.
World trade expanded faster than anticipated in 2025, 
as demand for AI-driven capex offset the effects of trade 
policy uncertainty and higher tariffs. The volume of world 
merchandise trade grew by 4.6%, compared to a forecast of 
2.4%. For the second consecutive year, Asian economies were 
the largest contributors to total world trade volume growth, 
accounting for 3.2 percentage points of the 4.6% total — or 
71% of the overall increase.
Trade in 2025 was also supported by investment in 
AI infrastructure, demand in emerging markets, fiscal 
and monetary expansion in advanced economies, and CREATING VALUE FOR ALL

India in FY2025–26: Domestic Demand Carries the 
Economy Forward
Against a challenging global backdrop marked by US tariff 
escalations and mounting trade policy uncertainty, the Indian economy demonstrated remarkable resilience during FY26. Real GDP growth accelerated to 7.6 percent, up from 7.1 percent in FY25, cementing India’s position as the fastest-growing major economy globally. 
This performance was underpinned by robust domestic 
demand, low inflation, and a broad pro-growth reform agenda. On the demand side, private consumption grew 7.7% year-on-year, supported by income tax reductions and rationalisation of GST rates. 
Economic activity was broad-based. On the supply side, 
manufacturing gained momentum, driven by the automobile and fast-moving consumer goods sectors. The services sector benefited from demand in retail trade, hospitality, transportation, and real estate. India also made progress in containing inflation, with the headline rate averaging 2% in FY26, down from 4.7% the previous year. 
India’s economic prospects for FY27 carry both 
opportunities and risks. Growth is projected at 6.6% by RBI, marginally revised down due to the effects of the Middle East conflict, which has pushed up global energy prices and disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. India nonetheless remains among the fastest-growing major economies globally.
Private consumption is expected to remain the primary 
driver of growth, though elevated global oil prices are likely to feed into domestic inflationary pressures. The GST rate reductions introduced in September 2025 are expected to partially offset this impact. Investment is projected to continue, supported by government capital expenditure, improved trade access through recently concluded free trade agreements, and a stable financial sector. 
India’s macroeconomic position, including foreign 
exchange reserves, a narrowing current account, and a path of fiscal consolidation, provides some buffer against external shocks. The pace of the renewable energy transition, the credibility of fiscal policy, and the implementation of newly concluded trade agreements will be factors that determine the trajectory of growth in the coming years.
Aditya Birla Group: In Our People We Trust
At the Aditya Birla Group, trust is built through experience. It is earned in thousands of everyday interactions—when people are given opportunities to learn, when careers progress on merit, when leaders are accessible, when commitments are honoured, and when employees know they can depend on the organisation through moments that matter.
Over time, these experiences shape how people feel 
about the Group. They influence whether talented individuals choose to join us, whether they see a future with us, and whether they are willing to invest their energy and ambition here over the long term.
The progress we have made across talent, leadership, 
culture and employee experience during the year reflects this enduring focus.
Trust in Competence: Helping people succeed from 
day one
The employee experience begins long before an individual 
settles into a role. The quality of hiring, onboarding and early support often shapes how quickly people become effective and how confidently they navigate a new environment.
During the year, we onboarded more than 11,700 
employees, including over 80 senior leaders, across businesses and functions. Structured hiring and onboarding processes, clear communication and timely feedback helped create a stronger experience for candidates and new joiners alike.We also continued to simplify the day-to-day employee 
experience through technology. Mobile-first onboarding and AI-enabled platforms such as AVA, which recorded more than 700,000 interactions during the year, improved accessibility, and delivered greater consistency at scale.
Capability building remains central to long-term success. 
Employees are more likely to perform with confidence when they have access to the skills, knowledge and support required to succeed. Through Gyanodaya, our Global Centre for Leadership Training, and other business-led initiatives, we delivered more than 280 programmes, reaching over 8,500 employees across technical, functional, behavioural and leadership domains. Ninety-eight per cent of employees accessed digital or blended learning through the Gyanodaya Virtual Campus (GVC). In addition, an intense 3-month group-wide learning initiative, the ‘Learning Fest’, engaged more than 39,000 employees, a fourfold increase over the previous year.
Managers play a critical role in shaping this experience. 
Through coaching, feedback and day-to-day guidance, they influence how employees learn, grow and navigate their careers. We therefore continue to invest in strengthening leadership capability across the Group.
Trust in Growth: Building careers across the Group
The strength of an organisation is often reflected in the opportunities it creates for its people. During the year, more than 6,400 employees moved across roles, functions, businesses or geographies. This is, by all accounts, a very significant number. These movements reflect the scale and diversity of opportunities available across the Group and reinforce our promise of ‘A World of Opportunities.’
Internal mobility also provides an important measure of organisational confidence. Of the 6,400+ movements during the year, more than 470 were across businesses. At senior leadership levels, cross-business mobility accounted for 15% of movements, strengthening leadership depth across the portfolio. Nearly 69% of senior management roles were filled through internal hiring, reflecting the quality and readiness of leadership talent developed within the Group.
These outcomes are supported by a disciplined approach 
to identifying and developing talent. 27% of employees form part of the Group Talent Pool. We have also built a strong pipeline of future leaders.
Our ability to attract high-quality talent continues to 
reflect the strength of our employer brand. Diversity hiring stood at 19% during the year, while retail businesses achieved 40% women hiring. Women’s representation within the leadership cadre increased by 8%. Seventy-four per cent of new hires were below the age of 35, with Gen Z accounting for 39% of all new joiners.  
The Group also received recognition across leading 
platforms including LinkedIn, the Top Employers Institute, Forbes and the Financial Times. 
Trust in Care: Supporting people and families
The employee experience extends beyond the workplace. Health, wellbeing and support systems influence how people feel, perform and engage over the long term.
Through our health, wellbeing and insurance initiatives, 
we supported employees and their families in meaningful ways. During the year, more than 8,600 counselling sessions were availed by employees, while workmen and staff accessed a further 3,100+ sessions, reflecting growing awareness and acceptance of mental wellbeing support. In parallel, over 3,400 eligible employees underwent annual health check-ups, reinforcing our focus on preventive care.
These efforts are translating into measurable outcomes. 
Among Mumbai-based employees, the proportion of individuals in the high-risk category, in terms of health, declined from 21% to 10%, while the low-risk category increased from 48% to 56%.
Employee sentiment continues to reflect this strong 
foundation. In our Annual employee survey, Vibes 2026, 96% of employees expressed pride in being part of the Group, 90% said they would recommend us as a great place to work, and 93% reported that their business inspires them to do their best work every day.Against a challenging global backdrop marked

Your Company’s Performance
FY26 marked a defining chapter in your Company’s journey 
as we completed our first full year of operations as an 
independent listed entity. The demerger has created a 
focused organization with the strategic flexibility, financial 
strength and governance framework required to pursue its 
growth ambitions. Supported by healthy cash flow generation 
and a strong ROCE profile, your Company is well positioned 
to pursue accelerated growth and create sustainable long-
term value for all stakeholders.
Over the years, our portfolio of brands has established 
leadership positions across their respective segments by 
consistently delivering compelling product propositions, 
strong consumer relevance, trusted brand equity and a presence across key price points and usage occasions. These 
enduring strengths have enabled us to build lasting consumer 
relationships and provide a strong foundation for future 
growth.
During FY26, we remained focused on strengthening 
every aspect of the business—from products and brands to 
channels and operations—with the objective of building a 
more agile, consumer focused and efficient growth platform. 
Our product strategy is centred on reinforcing our core 
and high-performing categories, expanding our evolving 
offerings built around growing trends of casualisation and 
premiumisation and building greater depth in adjacent 
categories. Alongside this, we sharpened our consumer 
engagement and go-to-market capabilities to enhance brand 
visibility, improve accessibility and elevate the customer 
experience across channels. 
The progress achieved during the year reinforces our 
confidence in the strength of our strategy and the resilience 
of our business model. As consumer demand strengthened 
and our execution gathered momentum, the investments 
we have made across our brands, capabilities and operating 
platform began to translate into business outcomes.
India’s Fashion Market Is Poised for Sustained Long-
Term Growth 
India’s fashion and lifestyle industry continues to offer a 
compelling long-term growth opportunity. Rising incomes, 
favorable demographics, urbanization and increasing fashion 
consciousness are reshaping consumer behavior, with 
apparel becoming an expression of identity, aspiration and 
lifestyle. Consumers today are seeking greater choice, better 
quality and more seamless access across physical and digital 
channels.
Industry estimates suggest that India’s apparel retail market could be more than ₹ 14 lakh crore by FY30, with 
organized retail growing faster than the overall market. The 
shift towards branded apparel, premiumization, omni-channel 
retail and digital commerce creates a favorable environment 
for companies with trusted brands, strong execution 
capabilities and differentiated consumer propositions.
While the near-term operating environment may continue 
to be shaped by geopolitical developments, inflationary 
pressures and fluctuations in consumer sentiment, India’s 
long-term consumption fundamentals remain strong. With its 
strong portfolio of brands, growing omni-channel ecosystem 
and focus on consumer-led innovation, Your Company is well 
positioned to fully leverage this opportunity.
FY26 Performance: Strengthening Momentum, 
Creating Value
FY26 was a year of disciplined execution and strengthening 
business momentum for your Company. Revenue grew by 
7% to ₹ 8,396 crore, driven by strong retail execution, healthy 
like-to-like (L2L) growth and broad-based performance 
across our brand portfolio. Momentum strengthened 
significantly in the second half of the year, with the business 
delivering double-digit growth as wholesale and other 
channels also witnessed improved traction. Strong secondary 
sales and a recovery in primary sales reflected an improving 
demand environment.
Profitability outpaced revenue growth, with EBITDA 
increasing by 13% and EBITDA margin expanding by 80 
basis points to 17.0%. This improvement was supported by 
disciplined cost management and sustained operational 
efficiencies, demonstrating the inherent strength and 
scalability of our business model.
Expanding and strengthening the retail network remained 
a key strategic priority. We added more than 300 stores 
(gross) during the year while upgrading existing locations to 
enhance productivity, reinforce brand visibility and improve 
the consumer experience. With a retail footprint exceeding 
4.9 million square feet, Your Company operates one of India’s 
largest branded fashion distribution networks.
Our distribution ecosystem enables seamless access 
across multiple touchpoints and comprises:
• 3,348 Exclusive Brand Outlets (including value-format 
stores)
• Over 39,500 Multi-Brand Outlets, with a strong presence 
in the innerwear category• More than 6,500 Shop-in-Shops across leading 
departmental store chains
• A strong digital presence across leading e-commerce 
marketplaces, complemented by our own brand websites
Importantly, the network is increasingly omni-enabled, 
integrating physical and digital channels to enhance 
convenience, improve inventory productivity and deliver 
a more seamless shopping experience. This capability 
continues to be a key competitive advantage and an 
important driver of future growth.
A Portfolio Built on Scale, Trust and Innovation
Lifestyle Brands
Our lifestyle portfolio—led by Louis Philippe, Van Heusen, 
Allen Solly, Peter England and Simon Carter—represents one 
of India’s largest and most admired house of brands. Built 
over decades on strong product propositions, deep consumer 
understanding and enduring brand equity, these brands hold 
leadership positions across their respective segments and 
remain central to your Company’s value creation proposition.
Collectively, the portfolio is well positioned to address 
India’s evolving consumption landscape across price tiers, 
occasions and lifestyle needs. The strength of the portfolio 
lies not only in the distinct positioning of each brand, but 
also in their complementary nature, which enables us to 
participate across a wide spectrum of consumer demand.
As preferences continue to evolve, we remain focused 
on strengthening brand salience and differentiation. 
Alongside reinforcing core categories, we are accelerating 
premiumisation, driving product innovation, expanding into 
adjacent categories and increasing participation in casual, 
active and occasion-led wear. These initiatives reinforce 
leadership in established segments while unlocking new 
avenues aligned with changing consumption patterns.
At the same time, we are strengthening brand 
engagement through sharper positioning, more differentiated 
communication and deeper consumer connect, particularly 
among younger cohorts. This is further supported by the 
ongoing enhancement of our retail experience through larger, 
lifestyle-led formats that improve brand expression and 
consumer immersion.
Taken together, these actions are strengthening the 
structural competitiveness of our portfolio and positioning 
your Company to participate more meaningfully in India’s 
expanding branded fashion opportunity over the long term.India’s fashion and lifestyle industry continues to

The emerging brands portfolio—comprising Van Heusen

Reebok, following its integration with Aditya Birla 
Fashion, has demonstrated strong scale-up potential, 
with revenues doubling and a significant expansion of its 
retail network over recent years. During FY26, the brand 
accelerated its expansion with the addition of over 50 
new stores, reinforcing its physical presence across key 
and newer markets. Growth has been led by improving 
traction in the retail channel, supported by e-commerce and 
wholesale. The brand continues to scale its presence through 
new product introductions across footwear and apparel, 
steadily broadening its consumer base and strengthening its 
positioning in the market.
Van Heusen Innerwear continues to build momentum 
in a structurally underpenetrated and largely unorganised 
category. Performance in the retail channel has improved, 
supported by rising confidence within the trade channel. 
The business is also gaining traction across e-commerce and 
quick commerce platforms, which are emerging as important 
contributors to reach and accessibility. Losses have reduced 
meaningfully during the year, reflecting better execution 
and operating discipline. The strategic focus remains on 
building product superiority, sharpening differentiation and 
strengthening consumer pull through repeat purchases, with 
a clear path towards profitability over the medium term.
American Eagle is steadily sharpening its positioning in 
India as a denim-led youth casualwear brand. The strategy 
is centred on deepening its denim credentials, pursuing 
calibrated expansion and strengthening operational 
efficiency. Continued investments in brand building and 
consumer engagement are enhancing awareness and 
reinforcing its positioning within the youth fashion segment, 
while driving a more focused and sustainable operating 
model.
Powering a Digital-First Culture Backed by 
Operational Excellence
Your Company continues to strengthen a culture anchored 
in operational excellence and digital agility across the value chain. This is led by tech-enabled processes, data-driven 
decision-making and a customer-centric operating model 
that enhances speed, responsiveness and efficiency. A 
strong focus on product strategy, supported by global 
sourcing capabilities, vertical integration into manufacturing 
and disciplined assortment planning, continues to drive 
consistency in execution and improvement in overall 
productivity.
A key strength of the operating model lies in its integrated 
and scalable supply chain ecosystem. A diversified vendor 
base enhances supply resilience, flexibility and speed-
to-market, while supporting responsiveness to evolving 
consumer demand. This is further complemented by strong 
capabilities in inventory management and replenishment, 
enabling efficient flow of products across channels and 
geographies. With more than 50% of the store network now 
omni-enabled, the omnichannel platform ensures a seamless 
and consistent consumer experience across touchpoints.
The retail expansion model remains largely asset-light and 
franchise-led, enabling scalable growth and deeper market 
penetration. These partnerships continue to play a critical 
role in extending reach while maintaining capital efficiency. 
This ecosystem is further strengthened by more than 10 
state-of-the-art manufacturing facilities, which serve as the 
backbone of operations. With an annual production capacity 
exceeding 30 million units, the network enables the Company 
to respond effectively to fast-changing fashion trends and 
demand cycles. The manufacturing workforce of over 16,000 
associates, the majority of whom are women, reflects a 
continued commitment to inclusive growth and workforce 
diversity.

MANAGING DIRECTOR’S MESSAGE
ADITYA BIRLA LIFESTYLE BRANDS LIMITED INTEGRATED ANNUAL REPORT FY 2025-26Dear Shareholders,
I am pleased to present the first Integrated Annual Report 
of your Company, Aditya Birla Lifestyle Brands Limited, for 
FY2025-26.
FY26 was a landmark year for ABLBL as we completed 
our first full year of operations as an independent listed 
company following the demerger. This was an important 
transition for the business, and I am pleased to share that we 
navigated it while maintaining continuity, preserving organ-
isational focus, and sustaining business momentum with 
minimal disruption. The year reflected the resilience of our 
operating model, the depth of our leadership capability, and 
the strength of the brands, systems, and execution prowess 
built over many years.
ABLBL today brings together a focused and powerful 
portfolio of some of India’s most trusted fashion and lifestyle 
brands. Our Lifestyle Brands portfolio includes Louis Philippe, 
Van Heusen, Allen Solly, Peter England, and Simon Carter, 
while our Emerging Brands portfolio features Reebok, Van 
Heusen Innerwear, and American Eagle. The portfolio leads 
its market segment with years of consistent innovation and 
execution.
ABLBL operates in India’s western wear market, a large 
and structurally attractive opportunity within the apparel 
industry. Growth in this market is being driven by rising 
incomes, urbanisation, premiumisation, the casualisation of 
work and everyday wear and the consistent shift towards 
branded fashion. The growing influence of digital platforms, social commerce and lifestyle-led consumption is further 
accelerating fashion discovery and demand. With its strong 
portfolio across formal, casual, athleisure, innerwear, and 
youth-led categories, ABLBL is well placed to benefit from 
these long-term consumption shifts.
FY26 Performance
ABLBL delivered a steady and resilient performance during 
FY26. Revenue grew 7% year-on-year to ₹8,396 crore, 
supported by healthy like-to-like growth of 9% and reset of 
other growth channels viz. ecommerce and MBOs. Business 
momentum specifically strengthened in the second half of 
the year, with the Company delivering double-digit growth 
as wholesale and other channels also witnessed improved 
traction.
Our profitability also improved YoY during the year.  
EBITDA grew ahead of revenue growth with 13% year-on-
year growth, with margins expanding by 80 basis points YoY 
to 17.0%. This improvement was led by operating leverage, 
gross margin improvement and continued high quality exe-
cution across the business.
This year, our priorities remained centred on building a 
stronger foundation for long-term growth. Our efforts were 
focused on reinforcing core categories, expanding high-po-
tential product lines, improving consumer relevance and 
creating more consistent experiences across retail and digital 
touchpoints.

The Lifestyle Brands portfolio remains the core strength of 
ABLBL. Louis Philippe, Van Heusen, Allen Solly and Peter En-
gland have played a defining role in shaping India’s branded 
western wear market over several decades. These brands 
have built deep consumer trust, strong recall, and a mean-
ingful presence across workwear, casualwear, occasion wear, 
and lifestyle-led dressing.
The scale of these brands reflects their enduring rel-
evance. Each of our key lifestyle brands has crossed the 
₹1,000 crore revenue milestone in the past, with two brands 
having exceeded ₹2,000 crore, placing them amongst a 
select group of apparel brands in India to have achieved such 
scale.
During FY26, the Lifestyle Brands portfolio delivered a 
resilient performance despite a challenging external envi-
ronment. Revenue grew 8% year-on-year to ₹7,154 crore, 
supported by strong retail execution, 8% like-to-like growth, 
and improving momentum across other key channels. 
The portfolio also maintained a strong profitability profile. 
EBITDA increased 9% year-on-year to ₹1,401 crore, with 
EBITDA margin at 19.6%. 
During the year, our brands sharpened their consumer 
proposition through product-refreshes, superior go-to-mar -
ket execution, and digital-first marketing. Campaigns across 
key occasions, travel, workwear, casualwear and festive 
helped strengthen consumer engagement and keep the 
brands contemporary and relevant.
We invested further in enhancing the retail experience. 
More than 175 Lifestyle Brand stores were revamped during 
FY26, creating fresher, more engaging and premium shop-
ping experiences. These efforts further enhanced store 
experiences, conversions and brand expression.
Continuous Product innovation remains at the core of our 
strategy and this year we consistently outperformed our -
selves on this key lever. Assortments were refreshed with a higher mix of natural and breathable blends, trend-led trims, 
sharper fits and craft-inspired detailing. These initiatives are 
helping the brands stay true to evolving consumer preferenc -
es while simultaneously reinforcing their leadership in core 
categories.
Leveraging their scale, equity and continued adaptability, 
our Lifestyle Brands remain well positioned to lead the next 
phase of growth for ABLBL.
Fueling the Next Frontier with Emerging Brands
Our Emerging Brands portfolio, featuring Reebok, Amer -
ican Eagle and Van Heusen Innerwear, scaled further and 
improved its operating performance during FY26. Exclud-
ing Forever 21, the portfolio delivered 8% revenue growth, 
supported by healthy retail momentum and a 13% like-to-like 
growth across the portfolio. Importantly, the portfolio also 
recorded strong profitability improvement, with EBITDA mar -
gin expanding by 370 basis points during the year. 
Reebok demonstrated growing momentum during FY26, 
delivering double-digit retail like-to-like growth. The brand 
added over 50 new stores during the year, taking its net -
work to more than 210 stores and strengthening its pres-
ence across both established and newer markets, especially 
small towns. The brand refreshed its product offering across 
footwear and apparel, with a sharper focus on the Indian 
consumer. Alongside this, stronger brand communication and 
the onboarding of a new brand ambassador helped improve 
consumer acceptance and visibility. As we move ahead, our 
focus will remain on scaling Reebok rapidly, improving store 
productivity and transforming it into India’s leading sports 
and lifestyle brand.
Van Heusen Innerwear continued to progress towards 
breakeven during FY26, with losses reducing significantly 
through the year. The business is now moving into a more 
growth-oriented phase, supported by improving channel mo-
mentum and a sharper operating focus. Retail performance was particularly encouraging, with like-to-like growth of over 
30%, reflecting stronger consumer acceptance and better 
execution at the store level. The brand remains focused on 
elevating product quality, driving new product introductions, 
strengthening differentiation and building a growing repeat 
consumer demand. As we move forward, our priority will be 
to scale the business in a disciplined manner while continu-
ing to improve profitability to reach sustainable earnings.
American Eagle further strengthened its position in India 
as a denim-led youth casualwear brand. During FY26, the 
brand expanded its retail footprint with the addition of over 
10 stores, taking its network to 70+ stores. The brand remains 
focused on building stronger consumer acceptance, deepen-
ing its relevance among young consumers and scaling profit -
ably. Leveraging the strength, product expertise, and global 
appeal of its parent brand, American Eagle is well placed to 
grow steadily in India’s youth fashion and denim-led casual-
wear market.
Building Scale, Creating Advantage 
A key strength of ABLBL is its robust pan-India distribution 
network. Our distribution ecosystem spans 3,348 Exclusive 
Brand Outlets, more than 39,500 Multi-Brand Outlets, with 
a particularly strong presence in innerwear and over 6,500 
Shop-in-Shops across leading departmental store chains. 
This is further complemented by a strong digital presence 
across leading e-commerce marketplaces and our own brand 
websites.
Our retail expansion strategy remains flexible, disci-
plined and return-focused. We will continue to scale through 
an optimal mix of franchise-led expansion and selective 
company-owned investments, guided by market potential, 
brand priorities and store-level economics. Our long-stand-
ing franchise partnerships remain a great source of strength, 
enabling us to expand rapidly yet efficiently.
ABLBL is also well positioned from a balance sheet stand-
point. The Company had net debt of ₹726 crore, with a clear 
roadmap to repay its debt in the near term through internally 
generated free cash flows. At the same time, we will continue 
to invest in growth, innovation, capability building, technolo-
gy and talent to strengthen the business for the future.
The Digital Leap
We continue to strengthen our digital and e-commerce ca-pabilities across all our brands, with the objective of creating 
a seamless, connected and consistent consumer experience 
across touchpoints. Built on our in-house e-commerce plat -
form, our digital ecosystem now includes dedicated brand 
websites, mobile applications and virtual stores, enabling 
consumers to discover, engage with and shop our brands 
with greater convenience.
During the year, we made significant progress in mod-
ernising our core technology infrastructure, enhancing data 
analytics capabilities and building AI-led solutions across key 
areas of the business. These initiatives are helping us improve 
decision-making, personalise consumer engagement, tailor 
content creation, optimise operations and deliver a more 
relevant and elevated customer experience.
Our omni-channel capabilities also scaled further, with 
more than 50% of our store network now fully omni-enabled. 
This allows customers to move seamlessly between online 
and offline channels, while enabling our brands to serve 
demand more efficiently across locations.
E-commerce remained an important growth channel 
during the year, delivering revenue of over ₹1,000 crore. This 
performance reflects the strength of our brand portfolio, 
the relevance of our offerings among digital consumers, and 
our strong partnerships with leading e-commerce platforms, 
complemented by our own digital assets.
Commitment to ReEarth Sustainability 3.0 Program
At ABLBL, sustainability is integral to the way we build 
brands, operate our businesses, and create long-term value. 
Through the ReEarth Sustainability Program, we continue to 
drive focused action across responsible sourcing, resource 
efficiency, circularity, product innovation, and value-chain 
transparency.
FY26 marks the beginning of the next phase of this jour -
ney — ReEarth Sustainability 3.0 Transformation. For ABLBL, 
this phase is about moving from adoption to deeper busi-E-commerce remained an important growth chan-
nel during the year, delivering revenue of over ₹1,000 
crore. This performance reflects the strength of our 
brand portfolioRevenue grew 8% year-on-year to ₹7,154 crore, 
supported by strong retail execution, 8% like-to-like 
growth, and improving momentum across other  
key channels.

ABOUT THE REPORT
We are pleased to present the first Integrated Annual Report 
of Aditya Birla Lifestyle Brands Limited (ABLBL). This report 
outlines our financial and non-financial performance during 
the year, together with our business objectives, strategic 
priorities, and long-term value creation approach. 
During the previous reporting year, pursuant to a Scheme 
of Arrangement, the Madura Fashion and Lifestyle business 
of Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail Ltd. (ABFRL) was de-
merged into a separate entity, Aditya Birla Lifestyle Brands 
Limited (ABLBL), w.e.f May 1, 2025. 
With the publication of our first Integrated Annual Re-port, we aim to provide stakeholders with a clear and com-
prehensive understanding of our business, strategic direction 
and our approach to managing key risks and opportunities as 
an independent entity.
Reporting Principles
This report is aligned with the International Integrated Re -
porting (<IR>) Framework of the Integrated Reporting and 
Connectivity Council (IRCC). This framework is the outcome 
of a joint initiative under the IFRS Foundation, involving the International Accounting Standards Board (IASB) and the 
International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB). The 
report highlights how value is created over time by pre -
senting our performance across the six capitals–financial, 
manufactured, human, intellectual, natural, and social and 
relationships.
The non-financial disclosures in this report have been 
prepared in accordance with the Global Reporting Initiative 
(GRI) Standards 2021 and are aligned with the Sustainability 
Accounting Standards Board (SASB) Standards, the Inter -
national Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) Sustainability 
Disclosure Standards, and the Securities and Exchange 
Board of India (SEBI)-mandated Business Responsibility 
and Sustainability Report (BRSR). Our reporting approach 
is also guided by the principles of the United Nations Global 
Compact (UNGC) and reflects our contribution towards the 
United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (UN SDGs).
The financial statements have been prepared in compli-
ance with the Indian Accounting Standards prescribed under 
Section 133 of the Companies Act, 2013. These statements  
also comply with the relevant provisions of the Act as out -
lined in the Companies (Indian Accounting Standards) Rules, 
2015 (including any subsequent amendments), Securities and 
Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure 
Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (SEBI Listing Regulations) read with all applicable SEBI Circulars, and the Secretarial 
Standard(s) issued by the Institute of Company Secretaries 
of India; and other accounting principles widely accepted in 
India.
Reporting Period 
This report provides an integrated overview of our perfor -
mance for the period 1 April 2025 to 31 March 2026. The 
disclosures presented in the report reflect development, 
performance trends, and strategic focus areas relevant to the 
reporting year.
Reporting Boundary and Scope 
This report discloses our financial performance for the 
consolidated business, covering subsidiary business entities 
listed in the Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report 
Section. The non financial reporting boundary includes the 
Company’s branded lifestyle businesses across key catego-
ries. These comprises of Lifestyle brands: Louis Philippe, Van 
Heusen, Allen Solly, Peter England, and Simon Carter; 
American Eagle; Sportswear: Reebok; and Innerwear: Van 
Heusen Innerwear. The reporting boundary includes Indian 
operations as mentioned below.

ABG SUSTAIN-ABILITY 3.0 is the Aditya Birla Group’s strate-
gic approach to enhancing enterprise value across the Group 
and its portfolio companies in both the short and long-term 
through a sustainability lens.
It builds on earlier phases of our journey: meeting reg-
ulations and establishing essential systems for responsible 
operations (Sustainability 1.0) and then strengthening perfor -
mance through the 4D approach* to identify material issues 
and set measurable, time-bound targets (Sustainability 2.0).
Sustain-ability 3.0 builds on these first two approaches and integrates our 2030 targets and 2050 ambitions, aligned 
with our Group Purpose and Values to act as a Force for 
Good.
Our priorities are shaped by internal and external sus-
tainability drivers that influence enterprise value, stakeholder 
expectations, and business resilience. These include:
• Customer and consumer expectations
• Access to financial capital
• Employee and community needs
• Brand reputation and trust• Evolving regulatory and disclosure requirements
Together, these drivers help us identify sustainability topics 
that are most relevant to our businesses and stakeholders.
Sustainability Themes
Our sustain-ability priorities are organised under three 
Group-wide themes:
Planet
We focus on reducing our environmental footprint and 
strengthening resilience. Key areas include climate action 
and decarbonisation, water stewardship, resource conserva-
tion, waste management, and the protection of nature and 
biodiversity.
People
Safety underpins all our business decisions. We promote 
physical and mental well-being across our workforce and 
value chains, with a continued focus on Zero Harm, inclusive workplaces, and responsible employment practices.
We also recognise our responsibility beyond the work -
place. We work to uplift communities by strengthening local 
well-being, supporting livelihoods and skills, and partnering 
to create safer, healthier, and more resilient communities 
wherever we operate.
Product
We advance circularity through design, reuse, and recycling, 
improve material efficiency, and expand greener and more 
responsible product portfolios to meet evolving market 
expectations.

Aligned with the Aditya Birla Group’s vision of building sus-
tainable businesses for long-term value creation, we contiune 
to embed sustainability at the core of our growth journey. 
As one of India’s leading fashion and lifestyle company, we 
recognise that the future of fashion will be shaped by climate 
resilience, responsible products, inclusive growth, and con-

Sustainability 1.0 focuses on process led approach, our 
journey was centered on establishing the foundations of 
responsible business practices. The focus was on strength-
ening compliance, improving resource efficiency, enhancing 
environmental management systems, and creating aware-
ness across the organisation. This phase laid the groundwork 
for integrating sustainability into day-to-day operations and 
decision-making processes.
Building on these foundations, Sustainability 2.0 shifts 
focus from process led to product led approach by scaling 
impact through stronger governance, enhanced ESG dis-
closures, renewable energy adoption, responsible sourcing, 
and operational excellence. Sustainability became increas-ingly embedded into business processes, enabling greater 
accountability, resilience, and stakeholder confidence across 
the organisation.
As we transition towards Sustainability 3.0, our focus 
shifts from building systems and scaling initiatives to creat -
ing impact and accelerating transformation. Sustainability 
3.0 represents a more integrated and forward-looking ap-
proach—one that combines business resilience with environ-
mental stewardship and social impact to create long-term 
value for stakeholders.
The evolving expectations of consumers, investors, regu-
lators, and communities are redefining the future of fashion. 
Sustainability 3.0 is designed to respond to these shifts by 
embedding climate action, responsible products, and inclu-sive growth deeper into business strategy, operations, and 
brand ecosystems.
What Enabled the Transition
Our progress across governance, renewable energy adoption, 
responsible sourcing, safety systems, ESG disclosures, stake-
holder engagement, and operational efficiency has created 
a strong foundation for the next phase of our sustainability 
journey. These efforts have strengthened organisational read-
iness and enabled us to scale sustainability from operational 
initiatives to enterprise-wide transformation.

As the business environment becomes more complex and 
rapidly evolving, uncertainty remains an intrinsic and ongo-
ing challenge. Organisations are required to navigate shifting 
market dynamics, regulatory changes, supply chain disrup-
tions, geopolitical developments, and climate-related risks. 
At ABLBL, strengthening operational resilience is central to 
our strategic approach to risk management. By embedding 
forward-looking practices, we enhance our ability to antici-
pate potential risks, manage uncertainties effectively, adapt 
to evolving conditions, and ensure business continuity.
Risk Management at ABLBL is supported by a well-de-
fined governance structure aligned with three lines of defence 
model, ensuring comprehensive oversight and accountability. 
This structure enables clear allocation of responsibilities, 
effective monitoring, and accountability at different levels of 
the organisation. The first line comprises frontline teams and 
operational leaders, including business unit heads and risk 
managers, who are responsible for identifying, assessing, and 
addressing risks that arise in day-to-day business activities. 
The second line comprises risk and compliance functions at 
the senior management level, which develop control pro-
cesses, frame policies, and monitor adherence to defined risk 
thresholds. The third line is represented by the independent 
internal audit function, which offers objective assurance on 
the effectiveness of risk controls, governance mechanisms, 
and compliance practices. Together, these lines help ensure 
consistent risk oversight, reinforce accountability, and sup-
port long-term value protection.Risk Management Process
We have instituted a strategically aligned Risk Management 
Framework to systematically manage and mitigate business 
risks in alignment with COSO’s enterprise risk manage-
ment principles. A dedicated team of professionals ensures 
effective implementation, with continuous monitoring of 
emerging risks. The framework sets out the company’s risk 
appetite, indicating the extent of risk it is willing to accept 
for identified risks. Our independent assurance mechanisms 
further strengthen risk governance structure. We conduct an-
nual internal audits to review adherence to risk management 
frameworks and compliance requirements, with periodic ad-
ditional evaluation of effectiveness and regulatory alignment 
by external audit. At the apex level, the Board-level Risk 
management and Sustainability Committee actively exercises 
the oversight of this framework, ensuring strategic alignment 
and robust risk governance.
Risk Identification & Categorization
We carry out a structured and rigorous evaluation of risks 
and classify them across strategic, operational, financial, 
environmental, and compliance-related segments, assess-
ing them based on their likelihood and magnitude. Root 
cause analysis further helps determine their possible effect 
on business operations, supporting informed, prudent, and 
data-backed decision-making.

whereas downside risks cover adverse impacts such as finan-
cial penalties, operational disruptions, and non-compliance 
with regulatory requirements.
Mitigation and Control Measures
Risk control measures are implemented in line with as-
sessment findings, with corrective actions integrated into 
standard operating procedures to avoid recurrence. This 
approach reinforces organisational agility and strengthens 
our preparedness to navigate evolving uncertainties. 
Continuous Monitoring and Review
Risk assessments are undertaken at defined intervals, with 
need-based reviews undertaken to address emerging risks 
and support timely mitigation. Where necessary, immediate 
reviews are conducted to ensure timely mitigation of poten-
tial risks. The framework is also subject to annual internal 
audits, supporting continuous improvement and readiness.
The Risk Management and Sustainability Committee 
meet twice a year to oversee the identification, assessment, 
and mitigation and provide strategic direction and oversight 
across the economic, social, and environmental risk dimen-
sions. This includes reviewing risk exposure and ensuring a 
structured response to emerging challenges.
Increasing Risk Awareness
In line with the ongoing Boad and Committee meetings, 
Independent and Non Executive Directors are regularly 
briefed on key developments through structured presenta-
tions covering business operations, strategy, risk manage-
ment framework, industry trends, and regulatory updates. 
Furthermore, risk management training is provided to the 
Board of Directors wherever significant revisions are made 
to the framework and is also extended to functional heads 
of new businesses to ensure a strong understanding across 
leadership. 
During the onboarding process, employees undergo 
comprehensive training on key risk areas such as safety, sus-
tainability, information security, and legal compliance. They 
are also provided specialised risk training based on their 
roles, such as occupational health and safety for relevant 
teams – reinforcing a culture of risk management across the organisation. Regular stakeholder engagement enables the 
governance body to gather meaningful feedback and better 
understand the concerns and expectations of diverse stake-
holder groups.
This process enables the governance body to remain 
well-informed about the potential impacts and related risks. 
By considering stakeholder perspectives, the governance 
body is better equipped to take informed decisions, man-
age risks effectively, and seize opportunities that align with 
stakeholder interests and contribute to sustainable develop-
ment. Quarterly risk updates from respective process owners 
further assist in identifying potential risks perceived at the 
process level. In addition, defined mechanisms for reporting 
value violations, ethics non-compliance, and whistle-blower 
concerns are in place, encouraging employees to report any 
risks they may observe through these channels.
Integrating Risk Management in  
Product Development  
At ABLBL, product development follows a defined approach 
that embeds risk considerations across the development 
lifecycle, enabling innovation while addressing potential risks. 
Through cross functional collaboration, teams jointly develop 
concepts and designs, drawing on diverse expertise to im-
prove product feasibility and market relevance. By integrat -
ing risk considerations throughout development, we aim to 
create products that are resilient, efficient, and aligned with 
business objectives and market needs.
More details on identified risks, corresponding mitigation 
measures, and emerging opportunities are provided in the 
‘Management Discussion and Analysis’ section of the report.Risk Assessment & Prioritisation
Following identification, risks are plotted on a heat map 
by evaluating their likelihood and severity. They are then 
classified as high (red), medium (amber), or low (green). This 
approach enables focused mitigation planning and helps pro-
tect business resilience. 
As part of our risk evaluation process, we undertake both gross risk and net risk assessments. Gross risk captures the 
inherent exposure faced by the business before controls are 
applied, while net risk reflects the remaining level of expo-
sure after mitigation actions and control measures are in 
place.
In addition to direct risks, we assess both upside and 
downside scenarios. Upside risks indicate unrealised oppor -
tunities related to growth, cost optimisation, and innovation,

OUR MATERIALITY
Taking into account the significance of risks, opportunities 
and sustainability impacts, we undertook a comprehensive 
double materiality assessment in FY 2023–24. We review our 
material topics annually to remain responsive to evolving 
business landscape and stakeholder expectations. To ensure 
our material topics remain closely aligned with evolving busi-
ness objectives and stakeholder priorities, we have initiated 
a detailed materiality assessment, which will be completed in 
FY 2026–27.
The assessment process involved engagement with a 
broad range of internal and external stakeholders, including 
senior management, employees, customers, academia, in-
dustry bodies, CSR partners, investors, suppliers, franchisees, 
and service providers. Through this engagement, we identi-fied actual and potential impacts of our business activities on 
the economy, environment, and society.
The approach was supported by sectoral research, market 
intelligence, and peer benchmarking to evaluate impacts 
across the short, medium, and long term. Using structured 
qualitative methodologies, material topics were systemati-
cally mapped on a materiality matrix to enable prioritisation 
and strategic alignment.
The outcomes of the assessment were reviewed and ap-
proved by the Board of Directors and further validated by an 
independent third party. The identified material topics have 
since been integrated into our Risk Management Framework, 
ensuring a coordinated and proactive approach to address-
ing key sustainability priorities.

water Opportunity 
and RiskThe fashion industry, known for its high levels of 
waste, pollution, and resource consumption, is seen 
as a major contributor to climate change. Excessive 
and inefficient use of resources can lead to higher 
operational costs, regulatory penalties, and negative 
environmental impacts, damaging brand reputation.
However, efficient resource usage and focus on raw 
materials and processes with lower environmental 
impact can result in cost savings, increased customer 
loyalty, the opening of new market segments and a 
stronger brand image.We are redesigning our products to increase 
wardrobe life, reduce environmental impact and 
enable reuse at their end-of-life stage.
Through our Sustainable Attributes, Sustainable 
Supplier Index and global assessment frameworks 
such as the Higg Index, we integrate sustainability 
across product life cycle and value chain. We also 
strengthen resource efficiency across operations 
through energy and water management measures 
such as solar rooftop systems, biomass briquettes, 
EV forklifts, rainwater harvesting, reuse of treated 
water from STPs, water-efficient fixtures and water 
positive projects.Positive GRI 302:

ChangeRisk The carbon footprint of a garment largely depends on 
the material. While synthetic fibres like polyester have 
less impact on water and land than grown materials 
like cotton, they emit more greenhouse gases per 
kilogram.
It is crucial to effectively manage emissions from 
across the value chain to limit the potential negative 
impact of climate changeWe have adopted various initiatives across Scope 1

value chain.
We are en-hancing the share of re-newable ener-

at both facility and product levels to effec-tively 
address climate change and its im-pacts.

Management 
and Circular 
EconomyRisk The repercussions of fast fashion are multi-faceted 
and need to be monitored closely. It contributes to 
significant pollution, resource depletion, and textile 
waste, with vast amounts of clothing ending up in 
landfills, leading to increased scrutiny from regulators.
It becomes crucial to effectively manage this waste 
and adopt the circular economy approach to maintain 
a positive brand image and gain customer loyalty.We continued to accelerate the transition from 
linear to circular models by integrating circular 
principles in our own operations and across the 
value chain.
Our in-house operations have achieved ‘Zero Waste 
to Landfill’ certification.
The entire non-hazardous waste in our facilities 
is either recycled or reused, and a small quantity 
undergoes composting, which is used as bio 
manure for farming.
Our collaboration with Germany’s GIZ focuses on 
material innovation, reducing inputs of harmful 
substances, increasing textile-to-textile recycling, 
developing alternatives to plastic packaging, and 
fostering traceability.
We have undertaken a commitment to recycle or 
upcycle 10% of products by volumeNegative GRI 306:

The year marked a pivotal milestone, laying the groundwork 
for our independent journey. Aditya Birla Lifestyle Brands 
Limited (ABLBL) from Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail Limited 
(ABFRL) in May 2025, represents an inflection point in your 
company’s growth story.
With a robust core business at its epicenter, and backed 
by high potential emerging brands portfolio, our company is 
well armored to scale leadership position in in the western 
and premium lifestyle fashion segments. 
Our portfolio is home to several of India’s most renowned 
and trusted brands in that continues to remain steadfast on 
expanding leadership through stronger consumer under -
standing for improved customer experience.
Our lifestyle brands form our core portfolio with Louis Philippe, Van Heusen, Allen Solly, Peter England and Simon 
Carter. Each brand catering to a different customer need 
across formal and casual categories. As these continue to 
deliver consistent and continuous growth, our endeavor is to 
strengthen this core business as a growth and cash engine. 
This ensures self-reliance for future expansion. 
Under emerging brands, we are driving expansion in high 
growth potential segments of sportswear, activewear and in-
nerwear as well as youth western wear. Our brands – Reebok 
(sportswear), Van Heusen Innerwear (activewear and inner -
wear), American Eagle (youth western wear) – are perform-
ing well, as we leverage our innovation and design capabili-
ties along with deeply penetrated distribution network.CONTRIBUTION

FY 2025-26 marked a year of strong performance and stra-
tegic progress, with our company delivering resilient growth 
despite a volatile market environment. The business demon-
strated robust execution across retail, sustained profitability 
improvement, and a well-managed transition to operating as 
a standalone entity.
For the financial year ended March 2026, we reported 
revenues of ₹8,396 crore, growth of 7.23% over previous year, 
backed by strong performance by lifestyle brands as well 
as emerging business. This enabled continued momentum 
in retail like -to-like growth of 9% year on year and a even 
stronger growth in small town network. 
Lifestyle brands generated revenue of ₹7,154 crore, grow -
ing by 8%, driven by growth across channels. Our network 
expanded by 230+ gross store additions, in line with our 
long-term strategic priorities, with EBITDA of ₹1,401 crore, 
and margin of 19.6%.
Our company generated Consolidated EBITDA of ₹1,429 
crore, registering a growth of 13% year on year. This was 
mainly driven by premiumization in portfolio brands, sup-
ported by improving profitability across emerging brands. 
Your company also witnessed accelerated adoption of 
technology and artificial intelligence across the value chain, 
enhancing efficiency across sourcing, merchandising, and 
customer engagement.
Consolidated EBITDA margin was at 17.0% for the year FY 
2025-26, expanding by 80 bps year on year.  These gradual 
improvements reflect our continuous efforts to leverage our 
operational as well as distribution excellence.
Our company delivered strong financial performance, 
with Profit After Tax increasing nearly threefold to ₹171 crore, 
reflecting a growth of 185% over previous year.
Net debt as on 31st March 2026 stood at ₹726 Crores 
with Debt: equity of 0.40.
During the year, our company generated operating cash 
flows before capex and security deposit of ₹ 450 crores, with 
a significant portion allocated to fund its accelerated store 
expansion strategy, adding 300+ new stores. 
We continue to build a strong and expansive retail foot -
print, with 3,348 exclusive brand outlets across ~800 cities 
and towns as on 31st March 2026. In addition, we continue 
to widen our presence beyond metro and tier-1 locations, with more than 560 stores in smaller towns. The visibility and 
accessibility are further enhanced with presence across more 
than 190 malls. Overall, with a footprint of ~4.9 million square 
feet as on 31st March 2026, we have kick started an aggres-
sive expansion engine for medium-term. 
Marking a strong start as an independent entity, the 
Board recommended a dividend of ₹ 0.50 per equity share 
for FY25-26, its very first year post-demerger, underscoring 
our company’s strong performance and commitment to 
delivering shareholder value.
Lifestyle brands business:
For FY2025-26, Lifestyle Brands reported revenue of ₹ 7,154 
Cr, reflecting a year-on-year growth of 8%. Growth was 
broad-based, with retail and wholesale channels contributing 
meaningfully. Retail, the largest contributor, grew by 8% YoY 
to ₹4,627 Cr, aided by healthy like-to-like growth of 8% and 
network expansion. Wholesale channel registered healthy 
growth of 9% over previous year, with revenues at ₹1,466 Cr. 
E-commerce generated revenues of ₹ 733 Cr, growing mod-
estly by 2% YoY, as the business recalibrated its digital strat -
egy while maintaining scale.  With strong focus on profitabil-
ity, EBITDA for FY 2025-26 stood at ₹1,401 Cr, an increase 
of 9% a year-on-year, mainly driven by operating leverage. 
EBITDA margin improved to 19.6%, a continued improvement 
in profitability highlighting disciplined cost management.
Lifestyle brands business accelerated on its growth plan 
to expand network with addition of +230 gross new stores, 
driven by a strong product-market fit in new markets and 
enhanced penetration across existing markets. 
Emerging brands business:

› Financial CapitalEmerging as a Focused Lifestyle Powerhouse
The year gone by marked the year of transformation – it is 
our journey of transformation as an independent company; 
following the demerger of the erstwhile Madura Fashion & 
Lifestyle business from Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail Limit -
ed (ABFRL). 
We inherit the strong legacy built by the Madura business 
over decades. Backed by a portfolio of iconic brands, we are 
well positioned to accelerate growth and create long-term 
value.
Our well-integrated ecosystem comprises owned manu-
facturing facilities, centralised warehousing, technology-en-
abled distribution networks, and an extensive retail footprint. 
This enables us to ensure consistent product quality, agility in 
operations, and faster time-to-market.
Sustainability is deeply embedded in our approach to 
fashion. As consumer preferences evolve towards more 
responsible and conscious choices, we are focused on ad-
vancing sustainable sourcing, resource-efficient operations, 
responsible manufacturing, and product innovation across our portfolio. Through purposeful action and continuous 
innovation, we aim to create enduring value for stakeholders 
while contributing to the development of a more sustainable 
and resilient fashion industry.
Manufacturing and Retail Capability
We operate a network of 11 manufacturing facilities across 
southern and eastern India, forming the foundation of our 
apparel manufacturing capabilities. Our manufacturing foot -
print includes six facilities in and around Bengaluru plus units 
in Bhubaneswar (Odisha), Thally (Tamil Nadu), Pulivendula 
(Andhra Pradesh) and a facility in Ramanagaram (Karna-
taka). These facilities primarily function as cut-and-sew 
garment manufacturing units and produce a diverse range of 
finished apparel, including formal shirts, casual shirts, trou-
sers, jackets, denim, innerwear, athleisure, and other lifestyle 
apparel categories.
Complementing our manufacturing capabilities is an 
extensive retail and distribution network that enables us 
to connect directly with consumers across India. During 
FY 2025-26, we strengthened our retail infrastructure by MANUFACTURED CAPITAL

expanding our network to 3,348 stores across nearly 800 
cities and towns, compared to 3,253 stores in FY 2024-
25. Our retail footprint grew to 4.9 million sq. ft. from 4.6 
million sq. ft. in the previous year, enhancing our ability to 
serve consumers across both metropolitan and emerging 
markets.
We continued to strengthen and diversify our manufac -
turing capabilities through targeted expansion projects and 
investments in operational excellence.  Our network is on 
track to produce nearly 30 million garments in FY2025-26, 
reflecting the scale and resilience of our operations. Keeping 
the manufacturing excellence our key focus area, during the 
reporting year, we achieved a record monthly dispatch vol -
ume of 27.12 lakh garments and eight of our manufacturing 
units achieved more than 80% efficiency.  The ABGL facility 
also achieved production milestones of 2.35 lakh trousers 
and 55,000 jackets in a single month, while the Aditree den -
im facility produced 8 lakh pieces and the MAL handbags 
business crossed 1.5 lakh units of production. 
Enhanced manufacturing flexibility and multi-product ca-
pabilities have also supported innovation, with new product 
volumes increasing from 7.55 lakh pieces in FY 2023-24 to 
15.9 lakh pieces in FY 2025-26. We continue to strengthen 
manufacturing agility through enhanced product fungibility, 
with approximately 10% of manufacturing capacity dedicat -
ed to developing multi-product capabilities. This enables facilities to switch between product categories and respond 
quickly to changing customer demand. As a result, our new 
product development capability has quadrupled over the 
last four years, supporting greater innovation, flexibility and 
speed-to-market.
Leading Product Sustainability
At ABLBL, sustainability has long been an integral part of our 
business approach and continues to guide the way we create 
value. As we grow as a leading lifestyle brands company, 
we are embedding sustainability considerations across our 
value chain - from product design and sourcing to manufac -
turing, distribution, and retail operations. We recognise that 
transforming the fashion industry is a complex and evolving 
journey, and while progress requires continuous effort and 
innovation, we remain committed to learning, adapting, and 
advancing responsible business practices. 
The adoption of technologies such as laser-based denim 
processing and digital tools like CLO 3D garmenting enables 
reduced water, energy, and material usage while improving 
efficiency and precision in manufacturing.  
Supported by a strong base of owned manufacturing 
facilities and trusted partners, we ensure greater control, 
traceability, and operational excellence, enabling the delivery 
of high-quality, responsible products at scale.›VAN HEUSEN CONTINUES to advance in sustainable 
fashion through low-impact and innovative materials, 
responsible sourcing, and resource-efficient manufacturing 
practices. The brand has expanded its portfolio of bam-
boo-blended shirts and tops for men and women. These 
products deliver lightweight, breathable, and moisture-wick -
ing comfort, while leveraging a fibre that typically requires 
lower water and pesticide inputs.
The brand has also increased the use of recycled materi-
als, including recycled polyester derived from post-consumer 
plastic waste, helping reduce reliance on virgin resources and supporting circularity across the value chain. Van Heusen 
continues to promote water-efficient dyeing and processing 
technologies that reduce water consumption and minimise 
chemical discharge, while also focusing on improving energy 
efficiency across manufacturing operations.
Responsible sourcing remains a key focus area, with 
increasing emphasis on traceable raw materials, including 
responsibly cultivated cotton and other sustainable fibre 
alternatives. Environmental performance across the supply 
chain is monitored through frameworks such as the Higg 
Index, particularly for Tier 1 suppliers.

›LOUIS PHILIPPE CONTINUES to advance its sustainabili-
ty journey with thoughtfully designed collections across 
categories. Its hemp-based sports casual shirts and trousers, 
offer breathable, durable garments with a significantly lower 
environmental footprint. Hemp cultivation requires minimal 
water and chemicals while producing more oxygen than trees, 
making it a standout sustainable fibre. Its T-shirt collection 
incorporates bamboo blends that offer natural antibacte-
rial, odour-resistant, moisture-wicking, thermoregulating, 
and UV-protection properties. Premium collections such as the GOLF Leisure Line and Tales of Masai feature TENCEL™ 
blended fabrics derived from sustainably sourced wood pulp 
and produced through a closed-loop process with high water 
and solvent recovery. Select formal shirts also incorporate 
Lyocell fibres sourced from FSC®-certified wood pulp, offering 
softness, breathability, biodegradability, and reduced envi-
ronmental impact. Through these material innovations, Louis 
Philippe continues to enhance product sustainability while 
maintaining the quality, comfort, and sophistication associated 
with the brand.

on high performers and roles that are pivotal to business

Nurturing Young Talent : Stride – Young Talent 
Management Programme 
The STRIDE Programme is Aditya Birla Fashion’s flagship 
young talent initiative, designed to identify, develop, and 
nurture future leaders for the organization. What began over 
two decades ago with the induction of Business Management 
Trainees (BMTs) has evolved into a robust, multi-disciplinary 
talent pipeline that today includes Fashion Management 
Trainees (FMTs), Chartered Accountant (CA) Striders, and 
B.Tech/M.Tech Striders. The programme continues to expand its reach by strengthening relationships with leading cam-
puses across the country while continuously evaluating and 
onboarding new institutes to build a diverse and future-ready 
talent pool.
Today, the STRIDE community comprises over 270 
Striders across multiple batches, streams, and business units, 
making it one of the organization’s most enduring talent 
pipelines. Managed centrally, the program ensures a consis-
tent and enriching employee experience through structured 
learning interventions, cross-functional exposure, mentoring, 
and continuous career development. Guided by the philos-
ophy of “Once a Strider, Always a Strider,” every participant 
remains connected to the program throughout their journey, 
with a dedicated HR team partnering with them at every 
stage of their career.
The success of the STRIDE Program is reflected in the 
journeys of its alumni. Many former management trainees 
have grown into leadership roles and today lead key func -
tions and businesses across Aditya Birla Fashion, reinforcing 
the program’s role in building a strong internal leadership 
pipeline. As the organization continues to evolve, STRIDE 
remains committed to attracting high-potential talent, fos-
tering innovation and agility, and developing leaders who will 
shape the future of Aditya Birla Fashion.

portfolio. The induction and learning experience were exe-
cuted with precision and consistency, ensuring every trainee 
received a strong foundation to begin their retail leadership 
journey.
The long-term impact of the programme is reflected in 
the success of its alumni. Over the years, graduates of the 
RYT Program have progressed into key leadership positions 
across the organisation. Many today manage high-per -
forming stores, lead regional operations, and contribute to 
strategic corporate and business roles that drive growth, 
transformation, and operational excellence.
Encouraged by the programmes strong outcomes and its 
contribution to leadership succession, we are further expand-
ing its investment in young talent. Building on the success of 
previous cohorts, the organization plans to onboard approxi-mately 175 Retail Young Talent trainees in FY 2025–26, creat -
ing a larger and stronger pipeline of future-ready leaders for 
its growing retail business.
By creating structured pathways for career growth and 
leadership development, the Retail Young Talent Program 
not only offers meaningful opportunities to young profes-
sionals but also strengthens organizational capability for the 
long term. The initiative remains a cornerstone of our com-
mitment to talent development, employability, leadership 
building, and sustainable growth.
Our investment in talent acquisition remained strong and 
deliberate, with a total hiring spend of ₹1.67 crore , reflecting 
our continued focus on attracting high-calibre professionals 
who align with our vision and values. During FY 2025-26, we 
welcomed 12,001 new employees into the organisation, of 
which 79% were women, reinforcing our sustained commit -
ment to enhancing gender diversity across all levels. We also 
continued to prioritise internal career growth, with 62.59% of 
open roles filled through internal mobility, demonstrating our 
belief in nurturing and advancing talent from within while 
building a future-ready and engaged workforce. 
Building a Future-Ready Leadership Pipeline 
At ABLBL, we firmly believe that organisations that succeed 
over the long-term are those that invest early in building 
their future leaders. Strengthening our leadership pipeline 
remains a strategic priority, and our Talent Councils play a 
pivotal role in ensuring leadership continuity through a struc -
tured and forward-looking approach to identifying, develop-
ing, and positioning talent for critical roles.  
In alignment with this, 100% of our permanent employees and workers received performance and career development 
reviews during both reporting period, reflecting our commit -
ment to continuous evaluation and growth. 
We leverage a robust 9-box performance–potential 
framework, further validated through Emerging Councils (JB 
6–9) and Leadership Councils (JB 4–5), to systematically 
identify high-potential talent and align them with future 
organisational needs. Through this process, we actively map 
talent to opportunities, create bridge roles, and establish 
clearly defined succession plans for key positions. This disci-
plined and proactive approach ensures that every strategic 
role is supported by ready-now or ready-soon successors, 
enabling ABLBL to operate with agility, resilience, and confi-
dence as we scale. 
Our performance management philosophy is designed to 
be holistic, inclusive, and developmental. Employees receive 
regular ongoing feedback from their performance manager 
and assessor through the ‘My Development Plan’ initiative. 
We have adopted multi-dimensional appraisal mechanisms, 
including 360-degree feedback, allowing employees to re-
ceive well-rounded, constructive insights from multiple stake-
holders This is complemented by a culture of continuous 
feedback, where agile and regular conversations between 
managers and team members support real-time performance 
improvement and development. We also emphasise team-
based performance assessment, recognising the importance 
of collaboration and collective outcomes alongside individual 
contributions. The employees’ performance manager and 
assessor provide feedback through our ‘My Development 
Plan’ initiative bi-annually. We also help employees set their 
individual goals and track their progress periodically.
Through these integrated efforts, we are not only 
strengthening our leadership bench but also fostering a 
culture of accountability, growth, and sustained high perfor -
mance across the organisation. 
 
Planned Actions to Strengthen Retention
At ABLBL, we believe that talent must not only be attract -
ed and developed but also meaningfully retained through 
enriching employee experiences and visible growth opportu-
nities. Our focus is on building a workplace where ambition 
is matched with a strong sense of belonging, enabling every 
individual to envision a long-term future with us. During 
the year, our voluntary employee turnover stood at 15.90%, and in response, we are taking deliberate steps to further 
strengthen retention outcomes. We are enhancing career 
pathing frameworks to provide greater transparency and 
clarity on growth opportunities across roles and functions, 
while also expanding internal mobility avenues to encourage 
cross-functional exposure and career progression.  
We continue to invest in strengthening managerial 
effectiveness, recognising the critical role leaders play in 
shaping employee experience and engagement. At the same 
time, we are deepening our focus on continuous learning, 
reskilling, and building future-ready capabilities to keep our 
workforce relevant and resilient. Leveraging people analytics 
and AI-driven insights, we aim to adopt a more predictive 
and data-led approach to retention and workforce planning, 
enabling us to proactively address potential risks and rein-
force a culture where our people feel valued, supported, and 
inspired to grow with us.

EDGE Assess Certification
At ABLBL, we have strengthened our commitment to gender 
equity by achieving the globally recognised EDGE (Equity, 
Diversity and Gender Equality) Assess Certification, be-
coming the first organisation in the Indian retail industry to 
be independently verified against international workplace 
gender equity standards. It is awarded only after a compre-
hensive, independent audit that evaluates how organisations 
perform across the most critical dimensions of workplace 
gender equity. 
As part of the EDGE Assess certification process, we 
underwent a deep, end-to-end assessment across four core 
pillars: 
• Gender representation across all levels of responsibility, 
from junior management to top leadership 
• Pay equity, including statistically robust analysis to iden-
tify any unexplained gender pay gaps 
• Policies and practices governing equitable career flows 
— spanning recruitment, promotions, leadership devel-
opment, flexible work arrangements, parental support, 
and workplace safeguards 
• Inclusive workplace culture, validated through anony -
mised employee perceptions and lived experiences 
The assessment combined quantitative workforce data, 
qualitative policy and practice reviews, and an employee 
survey, followed by an independent audit to verify accuracy, 
completeness, and integrity before certification was granted. 
The Certification places us among a select group of 
organisations worldwide that have subjected their gender 
equity journey to external scrutiny and transparency. The 
certification signifies that the company has established a 
credible and auditable baseline for assessing workplace 
gender equity, with core people policies and processes that
