Employee Engagement and Well-Being 
A Culture of Listening, Engagement & Well-Being
We view engagement and well-being not only as a stand -
alone initiative but also as a fundamental requisite to how 
we lead, connect, and grow as an organisation. We firmly 
believe that success to a sustainable business is rooted in a 
workforce that feels energised, valued, heard, and support -
ed. This belief is embedded in our continuous efforts to 
create meaningful listening channels and foster a culture of 
openness, trust, and shared accountability.Our enterprise-wide engagement survey, VIBES a flag -
ship initiative of the Aditya Birla Group serves as a corner -
stone of our listening strategy. It is administered annually 
across all business units and employee segments, covering 
100% of our workforce. During FY 2025- 26, the survey was 
conducted between 27 February and 14 March, witnessing a 
strong participation rate of 92%, resulting in a score of 85 on 
the employee engagement index. The survey covers aspects 
such as job satisfaction, purpose, happiness, stress manage -
ment and employee satisfaction against nine dimensions, 
including engagement, alignment, performance culture, 
managerial effectiveness, agility, employee experience, 
including engagement, leadership effectiveness, career de -
velopment, well-being, recognition, providing leaders with 
deep, actionable insights. 
The findings from VIBES survey have been instrumental 
in shaping both organisation-wide and team-level action 
plans, enabling us to continuously strengthen our peo -
ple practices and reinforce a culture of trust, growth, and 
accountability. To complement this, we deployed targeted 
business-specific surveys to capture contextual insights, 
including dedicated initiatives for frontline retail employees. 
We also conducted over 10 pulse surveys annually, using 
quick and interactive formats to gauge real-time sentiment 
across themes such as physical and mental well-being, 
engagement, and workplace experience.
In addition to quantitative tools, we place strong empha -
sis on qualitative feedback through structured Focus Group 
Discussions and post-survey feedback sessions, allowing us 
to gain deeper insights into key themes and employee ex -
periences. These insights are translated into clearly defined 
action plans across business units, supported by a strong 
governance framework with regular reviews to ensure ac -
countability and timely closure.
Beyond formal mechanisms, we have established multi -
ple platforms to encourage ongoing dialogue and real-time 
engagement. These include monthly CEO town halls, open 
forums with HR leadership, and regular team huddles that 
promote transparency, enable quick resolution of concerns, 
and celebrate achievements collectively. These interactions 
strengthen our organisational fabric, reinforce a sense of 
belonging, and ensure that every voice is heard.
Through this integrated approach, we continue to nur -
ture a culture where listening is continuous, engagement 
is intentional, and well-being is prioritised empowering our 
people to perform, grow, and thrive.Where Connections Thrive Beyond Work
For ABLBL, engagement is not an afterthought it is the 
heartbeat of our culture, shaping how our employees ex -
perience belonging, collaboration, and joy at work. Across 
our Business Units, engagement is woven into everyday life, 
creating moments that inspire creativity, strengthen bonds, 
and transform colleagues into a close-knit community. 
We believe that connections fuel performance, and every 
interaction is an opportunity to celebrate our people. This 
belief came to life through a series of thoughtfully curated 
initiatives across our businesses, each one rooted in our 
shared values yet infused with the unique spirit of every 
brand. This spirit of healthy competition thrived with the 
Madura Championship which brings in employees together 
for sports and non-sports events, fostering teamwork, cama-
raderie, and a shared sense of belonging.

Human Capital Development 
We view the development of our people as 
a strategic lever for long-term success. Our approach goes 
beyond traditional learning frameworks wherein, we aim to 
create an environment where growth is continuous, self-driv -
en, and deeply integrated into everyday work. Anchored by 
the Aditya Birla Group’s Continuing Education Policy (CEP), 
we provide structured pathways that enable our employees 
to build capabilities, broaden perspectives, and prepare for 
evolving roles. This aligns closely with our Employee Value 
Proposition of offering “A World of Opportunities”, empow -
ering individuals to chart meaningful and future-focused 
careers.
In an industry shaped by rapidly evolving consumer be-
haviour and continuous technological advancement, adapt -
ability remains critical. We view learning as an experiential 
journey, driven by real business challenges, cross-functional 
collaboration, and opportunities that push boundaries and unleash the potential of our workforce.
To support this, we have designed a comprehensive capa-
bility-building framework that addresses multiple dimensions 
of growth. We strengthen our retail workforce by equipping 
frontline teams with the skills and confidence needed to de-
liver exceptional customer experiences while preparing them 
for leadership roles. At the same time, we deepen functional 
expertise across roles, ensuring that our people are equipped 
with the knowledge and technical capabilities required to 
excel in an increasingly complex business environment.
Equally, we invest in shaping leaders who can inspire, 
influence, and lead with purpose, supported by programmes 
that focus on behavioural and leadership capabilities. As we 
look ahead, we are also prioritising the development of fu-
ture skills, enabling our workforce to stay aligned with digital 
transformation and emerging trends in the retail sector. 
We place equal emphasis on measuring the impact of 
learning, rather than just participation. Our approach focuses 
on tangible outcomes behavioural shifts, manager feedback, 
and sustained improvements in performance ensuring that 
learning translates into real, lasting value. During the year, 
we invested an average of ₹1901 per employee in learning 
and development, reinforcing our commitment to capabili-
ty building at scale. Our employees collectively completed 
73,974 hours of learning, reflecting strong engagement with 
development initiatives.
At ABLBL, we believe learning is not confined by formats 
or boundaries—it is continuous, immersive, and future-ori-
ented. It enables our people to think differently, perform 
better, and challenge conventional limits. More importantly, 
it prepares them not only for their next role, but for the 
opportunities of tomorrow by expanding mindsets, unlock -
ing potential, and redefining what is possible in the evolving 
world of fashion and retail.
Our learning philosophy is guided by a balanced under -

AI in Design / Patterns of God’ Collection by Allen Solly
To accelerate design-to-market timelines and strengthen trend responsiveness, Allen Solly introduced Generative AI 
into its design process through the launch of the ‘Patterns of God’ AI collection. The initiative was driven by the need 
to equip designers with practical AI capabilities, reduce creative lead times, and enable faster response to evolving 
fashion trends while maintaining product quality.
The L&D team, in close partnership with Allen Solly’s Creative Directors and Senior Design Leaders, identified the 
opportunity to embed Generative AI within the Design function. Following four months of research across LinkedIn, 
agencies and industry networks, the team partnered with GrowthSchool to design a focused 12-hour immersive learn-
ing curriculum. The programme covered leading AI tools including Midjourney, Leonardo AI, ChatGPT 4.0, DALL-E, 
ControlNet and Replicate, along with prompt engineering and practical applications for fashion design.
The intervention was designed not only as a training programme, but as an end-to-end capability-building initia-
tive. L&D managed tool subscriptions, enabled structured guided practice, and facilitated real-world application during 
training. Post-programme, designers across brands adopted Generative AI tools, supported by additional training on 
AI platforms, prompt engineering and Adobe AI integrations. This helped shift the designer mindset from hesitation 
and fear of AI to confident, creative adoption of AI as a working tool.
The impact was immediate and significant. For the Allen Solly team, the creation-to-in-store timeline reduced 
from 8–10 months to just 35 days, enabling a much faster route from concept to commercial launch. The initiative also 
marked a first-of-its-kind adoption of Generative AI in Design at this scale within the Indian apparel industry, strength-
ening Allen Solly’s position as an innovation-led and trend-responsive brand.
The commercial performance of the collection validated the effectiveness of the approach. Shirts achieved an 
average ROS of 0.37, close to the category average of 0.40, demonstrating competitive performance for a high-fash-
ion product. T-shirts outperformed the category benchmark, achieving an average ROS of 0.60 against the category 
average of 0.52. Overall, the collection proved that AI-designed fashion can perform at par with, and in select catego-
ries above, mainstream benchmarks building long-term organisational credibility for L&D-led AI capability building in 
Design.

Human Rights

Human Rights Commitment 
At ABLBL, human rights extend beyond compliance. They 
represent our commitment to fostering an environment 
defined by safety, respect, and fairness for every individual 
across our ecosystem.
We adopt a proactive approach to safeguarding hu-
man rights by strictly prohibiting practices such as modern 
slavery, child labour, forced or involuntary labour, human 
trafficking, and all forms of harassment. We maintain a 
zero-tolerance stance on discrimination and are committed to ensuring equitable treatment irrespective of race, caste, 
religion, colour, gender, sexual orientation, age, nationality, 
ethnic origin, disability, or any other legally protected charac -
teristic.
This uncompromising approach is embedded across our 
operations and upheld through robust governance frame-
works. We are also committed to protecting vulnerable 
and under-represented groups, including women, migrant 
workers, minorities, and indigenous communities. During FY 
2025–26, there were no reported incidents involving indige-
nous communities, reflecting our strong preventive focus.
Additionally, we uphold fair working conditions and 
equitable remuneration practices through regular monitoring 
of working hours, adherence to overtime norms, and ongoing 
engagement with employee and worker representatives to 
ensure safe, compliant, and inclusive workplaces across all 
locations.
Our responsibility extends beyond the organisation, en-
compassing our broader value chain. All suppliers, contrac -
tors, and business partners adhere to our human rights stan-
dards as a fundamental condition of engagement, promoting 
ethical conduct across all touchpoints.
Through these structured and sustained efforts, we strive 
to ensure that respect for human rights remains deeply em-
bedded in the way we operate, engage, and grow.

ly, no remediation actions were required.

Grievance Redressal
We have established a transparent, accessible, and robust 
grievance redressal system that ensures every issue is ad-
dressed with fairness, confidentiality, and accountability.
We have also institutionalised robust mechanisms to en-
sure a safe and respectful workplace. An Internal Complaints 
Committee, constituted in line with the POSH Act, is respon-
sible for the timely and effective handling of complaints. Em-ployees have access to multiple reporting channels, including 
a toll-free hotline, enabling them to raise concerns directly 
with the ABLBL Value Committee, HR, or their managers 
with confidence.
Our grievance framework is anchored in a fully digital, 
end-to-end complaint management system, enabling the 
efficient handling of Code of Conduct violations and Preven-
tion of Sexual Harassment (POSH) cases. Each business unit 
is supported by dedicated and trained committees for both 
Values-related matters and POSH, with the latter comprising 
an external member in accordance with statutory require-
ments. These committees conduct thorough and unbiased investigations, ensuring that every complaint undergoes 
appropriate scrutiny prior to resolution.
All grievances are routed through Integrity Matters, our 
third-party managed platform, which allows reporting via 
multiple channels, including email, telephone, website, and 
postal communication. This ensures both accessibility and 
strict confidentiality, while enabling complete traceability of 
each case. To maintain consistency and control, complaints 
are not accepted through informal or offline channels. De-
fined timelines are adhered to, with resolution of Values-re-
lated cases within 30 days and POSH cases within 90 days, 
aligned with regulatory norms.
AI-Powered End-to-End Go-To-Market –  
‘Ice Cream Man’ Collection by Simon Carter
Building on the success of L&D’s AI in Design training programme, Simon Carter scaled AI adoption across the 
complete go-to-market lifecycle for the ‘Ice Cream Man’ collection. The initiative expanded the use of AI beyond 
design into product development, marketing and visual merchandising, making it one of the most comprehensive 
AI-integrated launches in the organisation’s history.
The objective was to reduce traditional GTM lead times of 3–6 months and demonstrate measurable business 
impact through end-to-end AI integration. L&D enabled teams across Design, Product, Marketing and Visual Merchan-
dising to independently apply AI tools across critical stages of the launch, converting the training intervention from a 
capability-building programme into a business transformation lever.
AI was embedded at each stage of the GTM process. During the design stage, concept creation was completed in 
just 1 day, compared to the earlier timeline of 30 days, resulting in a 97% reduction in lead time. In the product stage, 
AI-assisted design-to-product workflows reduced timelines by nearly 50%, bringing the cycle down from 150 days to 
75 days. The impact extended into campaign development and retail execution. Marketing teams used AI-powered 
shoot and campaign creation workflows to reduce campaign shoot timelines by 67%, from 12 weeks to 4 weeks, while 
lowering campaign shoot costs by approximately 90%. Visual merchandising teams also used AI tools to create store 
window concepts in just 1 day, compared to the earlier timeline of 2 weeks.
A key enabler was L&D’s focus on prompt engineering, which helped teams generate high-quality outputs in-
dependently across functions. This built cross-functional AI capability across four business areas  Design, Product, 
Marketing and Visual Merchandising and demonstrated that AI could be meaningfully integrated into real business 
workflows, not just explored as a standalone learning initiative.
The commercial performance of the ‘Ice Cream Man’ collection strongly validated the approach. The collection 
achieved 68% full-price sell-through, outperforming the industry benchmark of 55% for best-seller products. It also 
delivered an ROS of 1.3, significantly higher than the industry benchmark of 0.5 for best-seller products.
Overall, the initiative established the ‘Ice Cream Man’ collection as a landmark success and set a new bench-
mark for AI-enabled fashion GTM. By delivering measurable improvements in speed, cost efficiency, cross-functional 
capability and commercial performance, the programme reinforced L&D’s strategic role in embedding AI across the 
business and positioned ABLBL as an innovation leader in the fashion industry.HUMAN CAPITAL

Occupational Health and Safety 
At ABLBL, safety is a core pillar of our operational excellence 
and a critical enabler of sustainable growth. Anchored in our 
sustainability programme, ReEarth – For Our Tomorrow, we 
are committed to creating a safe, secure, and resilient work -
place that supports employee wellbeing while strengthening 
engagement and retention.
Safety Governance
We realise that a workplace that is safe and sound is essen-
tial to attract talented and engaged employees. To ensure 
safety, we have a dedicated Business Review Council (BRC) 
at the board level that oversees the overall implementation 
of our safety policies and reviews its performance quarterly. Our three-tier approach to safety performance includes an 
initial review by the site safety committee followed by the 
business safety committee/sub-committee and finally by the 
Business Review Council. The CSO monitors OHS perfor -
mance and communicates with the Management Committee 
and RMSC. Further, the RMSC provides oversight on safe-
ty-related matters and strategies. 
Safety governance is reinforced through site-level com-
mittees comprising equal representation from management 
and employees, fostering collaboration and shared owner -
ship. Workers actively contribute to risk assessments and 
improvement initiatives, while regular meetings are held to 
review performance, address risks, and drive accountability. 
A structured incident reporting and investigation frame-
work ensures that all incidents and near misses are promptly 
reported, recorded, and addressed. Incidents are escalated 
to the relevant area in-charge, safety officer, HR manager, 
and facility manager, in line with the defined reporting matrix 
communicated across the organisation. All events are logged 
through the ReEarth Sustainability Portal, with designated 
personnel responsible for timely reporting based on incident 
severity.
Worker Participation and Consultation
We actively promote meaningful worker participation and 
consultation across all stages of our OHS Management 
System, including its development, implementation, and 
evaluation. This is enabled through structured mechanisms 
that encourage engagement, ownership, and continuous 
feedback.
A formal Joint Safety Committee is established across all 
manufacturing and warehouse facilities, with equal repre-
sentation from management and worker representatives 
are elected at regular intervals, ensuring fair representation 
and active participation. The committee meets monthly at 
manufacturing facilities and once every quarter at warehouse 
locations to review OHS performance, discuss hazards, and 
drive continuous improvement.
In addition, our Safety Observation Programme fosters 
proactive engagement between supervisors, line managers, 
and workers on the shop floor. Observations on safe and 
unsafe behaviours and conditions are systematically record-
ed and analysed, with insights fed into the HIRA process and 
corrective action plans.
We also provide multiple channels for hazard and near-miss reporting, including direct reporting to supervisors, 
safety registers, and digital platforms. All reported con-
cerns are acknowledged, investigated, and addressed, with 
feedback provided to the reporting individual, reinforcing 
transparency and trust.
Managers and line leaders actively engage with workers 
to identify risks and encourage open reporting of safety 
concerns. Site-level safety committees promote employee 
participation and shared responsibility in maintaining safe 
workplaces.
Our Approach to Occupational Health  
and Safety
During FY 2025–26, we strengthened our Occupational 
Health and Safety (OHS) framework to ensure comprehen-
sive coverage across all operational sites, aligned with appli-
cable legal and regulatory requirements. Standard Operating 
Procedures (SOPs) have been systematically implemented 
across factories, warehouses, and retail locations, driving 
consistency and discipline in safety practices across the 
organisation. 
Our approach is anchored in continuous risk assessment, 
proactive mitigation, and ongoing performance improve-
ment. This has delivered tangible outcomes, including zero 
workplace fatalities during the year, reflecting the robustness 
of our systems and the strong commitment of our workforce.
Following any incident, an investigation team is consti-
tuted to conduct root cause analysis, with corrective and 
preventive actions implemented within defined timelines to 
prevent recurrence. This process is supported by digital tools, 
including QR-based reporting systems, which enable em-
ployees to easily raise safety concerns and enhance reporting 
transparency.
To strengthen prevention and mitigation, we enhanced 
the reporting and monitoring of safety observations and 
near-miss incidents through our digital EHS systems. Guided 
by the Heinrich Safety Triangle principle, we adopted a pro-
active approach focused on early identification and resolu-
tion of risks before they escalate into Lost Time Injuries (LTIs) 
or serious incidents.
We conducted regular internal and external safety audits, 
inspections, and compliance assessments to identify gaps 
and implement corrective and preventive actions (CAPA). 
Structured risk registers were maintained to track critical 
risks and infrastructure improvements, with high-priority observations reviewed through management governance 
forums to ensure timely closure.
To further strengthen operational control, high-risk and 
non-routine activities are governed by a structured Work 
Permit System, ensuring appropriate safeguards are in place 
before work begins. The Lockout–Tagout (LOTO) system is 
rigorously implemented to control hazardous energy, sup-
ported by engineering controls. In addition, clear Operating 
Control Procedures (OCPs), regular training, and a well-de-
fined Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) matrix ensure the 
safe execution of tasks across all functions.
Periodic self-assessments are also conducted to evaluate 
preparedness in critical areas such as fire safety and emer -
gency response, reinforcing our commitment to continuous 
improvement and operational resilience.
Routine safety inspections are conducted at defined 
intervals across shop floor and facility levels, using stan-
dardised checklists covering equipment, housekeeping, PPE 
compliance, and safe work practices. Annual internal audits, 
undertaken by qualified and cross-functional teams, assess 
the overall effectiveness of the OHS management system, 
with findings categorised by risk severity- high, medium, or 
low to enable prioritised action. Key observations, particular -
ly high-risk issues, are escalated to senior leadership through 
established governance mechanisms, ensuring timely deci-
sion-making and effective closure.
This framework is further strengthened through exter -
nal audits conducted at selected facilities by independent 
third-party bodies and ISO certifying agencies, providing 
objective validation of compliance and implementation 
effectiveness. 
Safety is embedded across the entire lifecycle of our op-
erations, including new projects, expansions, modifications, 
and acquisitions. Each initiative undergoes comprehensive

Driving Culture Through Safety 2.0
To further embed a proactive safety culture, ABLBL in-
troduced the Safety 2.0 initiative across all facilities. This 
programme focuses on strengthening risk management, 
enhancing infrastructure, improving compliance, and acceler -

Monthly safety review meetings led by senior manage-

critical risks, and ensure timely closure of gaps. Leader -

and allocation of resources for safety initiatives, fostering 
accountability and maintaining high safety standards across

Safety Management System
Our OHS Management System is aligned with the ABG TS 14 
framework, designed to enable a Zero Harm environment. It 
encompasses eight core elements: leadership commitment; 
policy and strategic objectives; organisation, resources and 
competence; risk evaluation and management; planning, 
standards and procedures; implementation, monitoring 
and reporting; inspection and assurance; and management 
review. These elements are supported by detailed sub-com-
ponents to ensure rigour, consistency, and accountability at 
every level. All our operational sites, employees and workers 
are fully covered by an occupational health and safety man-
agement system that complies with legal requirements and 
recognised standards.
Risk Assessment and MonitoringOur Hazard Identification and Risk Assessment (HIRA) 
process provides a comprehensive framework for evaluating 
risks across physical, electrical, fire, chemical, ergonomic, and 
psychosocial domains. Identified hazards are assessed based 
on their level of significance, and appropriate control mea-
sures are implemented in line with the hierarchy of controls, 
including elimination, substitution, engineering controls, 
administrative controls, and the use of PPE.
HIRA is reviewed periodically, following incidents, and 
prior to the introduction of new activities, ensuring its ongo-
ing relevance and effectiveness. Insights from near-miss and 
incident investigations are systematically fed back into the 
process to drive continuous improvement.
This internal framework is further strengthened through 
external assessments at selected sites, validating alignment 
with ISO 45001:2018 standards. In addition, a dedicated 
monitoring application tracks critical parameters such as 
temperature, pressure, and fire system performance, enabling 
real-time alerts and timely interventions to proactively man-
age risks. During the reporting year, 11 factories underwent 
safety assessments, including ISO 45001 surveillance audits, 
while 582 stores were evaluated through safety audits, and 2 warehouses were assessed for safety, fire, and electrical 
compliance.

sites. This data is validated and reviewed monthly by safety

Implementation of Double-Handed Operation  
in End Cutting Machine
In our fabric manufacturing operations, end cutting machines posed a significant risk of cut injuries to operators. 
While a 360° guard had been installed as an initial engineering control, incident analysis revealed that operators were 
occasionally bypassing this safeguard to manually adjust misaligned or stuck fabric while the machine was still in 
operation. This highlighted a critical behavioural risk that required a stronger, design-led intervention.
We identified the hazard through our Hazard Identification and Risk Assessment (HIRA) process and further validated 
it through safety observations and incident analysis. Although the 360° guard provided protection during normal op-
eration, root cause analysis confirmed that unsafe manual interventions during machine movement were the primary 
cause of injuries.
In line with the hierarchy of controls, we upgraded our approach by introducing a Double-Handed Operation Control 
system. This engineering modification requires operators to engage both hands simultaneously on designated controls 
to run the machine, ensuring that their hands remain away 
from the cutting zone at all times. Releasing either control 
immediately stops the machine and brings it to a safe idle 
state, allowing fabric adjustment only when it is safe.
The solution was developed in consultation with machine 
operators to ensure practicality and ease of use. All operators 
were trained on the revised operating procedure, and imple-
mentation was supported through regular inspections and 
behavioural observations to ensure sustained compliance and 
effectiveness. The existing 360° guard was retained, resulting 
in a robust dual-layer safety system.
The initiative led to a measurable reduction in cut-related in-
juries and strengthened overall safety performance in cutting 
operations.Fire Safety Marshal Training Programme
The Safety Marshal Programme was launched with a clear objective to equip every store-level employee with essen-
tial fire safety knowledge and hands-on skills to operate fire extinguishers effectively. The initiative followed a tiered 
training model, beginning with centralised sessions for 
Regional Business Managers and cascading down to 
Area Business Managers, Store Managers, and Customer 
Care Associates. This ensured consistent and practical 
knowledge transfer across all levels. The programme’s 
impact was powerfully demonstrated during a real-life 
fire incident. Trained team members responded swiftly 
locating extinguishers, acting calmly, and successfully con-
trolling the fire, preventing panic and major damage. Their 
quick action validated the programme’s effectiveness 
and life-saving potential. Now a cornerstone of our safety 
culture, the Safety Marshal Programme goes beyond 
compliance. It instils confidence, accountability, and pre-
paredness among employees, reinforcing our commitment 
to workplace safety and emergency readiness. We remain 
dedicated to scaling such initiatives to ensure safety 
remains integral to our organisational ethos.

Strengthening Circularity in Fashion  
Embedding sustainability principles across our 
business and product portfolio remains central to our 
strategy. As we advance our circular fashion journey, 
sustainability is integrated across the product life-
cycle—from design and material selection to manu-
facturing, distribution, consumer use and end-of-life 
management. Our focus is on extending garment life-
cycles through durable design, responsible sourcing, 
resource-efficient production and innovative material 
choices, including recycled and lower-impact fibres.
We are also strengthening circularity through 
garment take-back initiatives and partnerships that 
support the reuse, recycling and repurposing of tex -
tiles, helping divert waste from landfills and reduce 
dependence on virgin resources. Recognised by the 
Ellen MacArthur Foundation’s Circular Design for 
Fashion, our approach is underpinned by strong governance, 
clear accountability and continuous improvement. Through 
these efforts, we are reducing our environmental footprint 
while creating long-term value for customers, communities 
and the planet.
Accelerating Circularity in Indian Textiles: 
Aditya Birla Fashion–GIZ develoPPP Project 
To advance circularity in the Indian textile and apparel sector, 
Aditya Birla Fashion partnered with GIZ Germany under the 
three-year develoPPP programme. Launched in 2021, the 
Approaches for Circular Textiles and Apparel Industry in India 
(ACT) project promotes circular practices through innovation, 
capacity building and collaboration across the value chain. 
Implemented with the Centre for Environment Education 
(CEE) and supported by the International Council for Circular 
Economy (ICCE) as knowledge partner, the initiative brings 
together industry and development expertise to drive sec -
tor-wide change.
Guided by a multi-stakeholder Steering Committee, the 
project focuses on strengthening industry capacity to adopt 
circular business practices. Key areas include reducing harm-
ful inputs, advancing textile recycling, extending product lifecycles through reuse, and promoting alternative materials 
and renewable energy. Contributing to SDGs 5, 8, 10, 12, 13 
and 17, the initiative supports a more inclusive, resource-effi-
cient and low-waste textile value chain.
Key Components & Milestones 
CIRCULARITY BASELINE ASSESSMENT 
To develop a comprehensive understanding of circularity 
within the textile industry, a pan-India assessment was car -
ried out to map key challenges, identify high impact areas, 
and define intervention priorities. 
The survey brought together insights from over 90 stake-
holders, including textile mills, garmenting units, processing 
and dyeing units, waste processing agencies, brands, retail 
stores, consumers, government ministries and associations, 
as well as academic institutions. The findings from this com-
prehensive assessment were officially launched at the Inter -
national Circular Economy Forum (ICEF) held in New Delhi. 
Innovation Challenge 
An innovation challenge was carried out on GIZ leverist plat -
form to identify scalable circularity solutions. The initiative received 87 submissions, out of which 09 were shortlisted for 
industry adoption following evaluation by an external jury. All 
innovations were compiled into a booklet that was officially 
launched at Bharat Tex in the presence of the Joint Secretary 
and senior representatives from Aditya Birla Fashion and GIZ. 
Demonstration Project 
We identified three circularity projects emerging from the in-
novation challenge and successfully implemented in brands. 
While the remaining projects were made accessible to indus-
try stakeholders to encourage wider adoption and scalability. 
Capacity Building on Circularity 
A comprehensive training curriculum was developed, consist -
ing of three tailored modules for the leadership team, middle 
management, and trainers. The programme was implement -
ed across nine key textile clusters in India, reaching 426 
participants from diverse stakeholder groups. This included 
a two day Training of Trainers (ToT) programme, covering 
Circular Fashion, Advanced Waste Management, Circular 
Business Models, and Innovative Circular Strategies, resulting 
in the creation of a pool of 26 certified trainers from senior 
and middle management levels. 
Development of Guidelines 
The ‘Stitching the Circle’ Circularity Guidelines and Manifesto 
were developed through an extensive stakeholder engage-
ment process, including seven focus group consultations across textile clusters in India and the broader textile value 
chain. The process brought together over 300 stakeholders, 
along with a dedicated 24 member working group repre-
senting brands, academia, recyclers, textile mills, NGOs, and 
innovators. Guided by three key priorities: strong stakeholder 
engagement, key performance metrics for benchmarking, 
and dissemination to industry and government- the draft was 
refined through multiple consultations and finalised by the 
working group. The guidelines were officially released at the 
Sankalp Summit and Bharat Tex, marking an important step 
in advancing circularity across the industry. The guideline 
establishes circular economy practices clearly and offers a 
structured pathway to reduce dependency on virgin resourc -
es and promote waste-to-value initiatives. 
Communications 
The Aditya Birla Fashion-GIZ collaboration gained significant 
visibility through coverage across leading media outlets, 
industry conferences, global forums, and social media plat -
forms. The Circular Business Guidelines were disseminated 
with over 5,000 stakeholders across the Indian textile sector, 
contributing to broader industry awareness and engagement 
on circularity.

Measures are in place to continuously enhance security sys-

Information security governance is designed such that 
each business unit’s IT team reports to the respective Busi -
ness Heads as well as the Chief Information Security Officer 
(CISO). IT and security functions operate independently 
from the Central IT framework for specific business entities, 
with separate governance and review mechanisms in place

reporting structure for information security ensures that the 
CISO reports to the Chief Digital and IT Officer, who pro -
vides regular updates to the Board-level Risk Management

egy and monitoring are overseen by the management-level 
Information Security Committee, comprising six members. 
Oversight includes periodic corporate reviews to ensure 
consistency and effectiveness. Data privacy governance 
is embedded within the overall compliance framework, 
aligning it with broader regulatory and risk management 
processes. 
The CISO has developed a risk assessment framework for 
Personally Identifiable Information aligned with our compa-
ny’s overall risk assessment approach. Risks are assessed on 
an annual basis, and mitigation measures are implemented 
as required. All the staff are expected to report any security 
incidents and support related investigations as necessary. 
Information Security Controls 
Our IT systems and infrastructure are aligned with the ISO 
27001 Information Security Management System standard 
and the NIST 853 framework, reflecting a strong commitment 
to safeguarding information assets. During the year, we up-
graded the certification to ISO 27001:2022. To sustain these 
standards, we conduct regular internal audits and reviews 
across IT systems and infrastructure to ensure full compliance 
with the Information Security Policy. These reviews support 
consistent adherence and help preserve system integrity 
across the organisation. We also undertake independent 
external audits aligned with ISO 27001 to validate both tech-nical controls and policy implementation. 
During the year, we strengthened our cybersecurity pos-
ture by reinforcing protection and monitoring across critical 
areas of our IT environment. We have upgraded our Endpoint 
security from traditional antivirus systems to next generation 
Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR), enabling real time 
and response to cyber threats. Security of public facing web-
sites has been reinforced through advanced controls, including 
DNS security measures to block malicious communications 
and limit ransomware attacks, along with the deployment of 
Cloud Web Application Firewall (WAF) solutions to safeguard 
e commerce and other internet facing platforms. 
Our cloud security capabilities have also been enhanced 
by improving visibility and risk management across AWS 
workloads, identities, and configurations. In parallel, identity 
protection has been reinforced through the implementation 
of next generation Privileged Access Management solutions, 
along with multi factor authentication controls for internal 
users and third party contractors, ensuring tighter control 
over access across the ecosystem. 
Our security framework is built on a defence-in-depth 
approach, incorporating multiple layers of controls across 
key areas such as physical infrastructure, network security, 
identity and access management, applications, endpoints, 
and data. These controls are continuously supervised 
through Security Incident and Event Management (SIEM) 
systems, supported by a dedicated security operations team. 
Additionally, cyber threat intelligence services are utilised 
to detect emerging risks, enabling timely updates, patching, 
and preventive actions. 
We perform annual vulnerability assessments and 
penetration testing using both internal teams and external 
experts. We also conduct red teaming exercises that simulate 
real life attack scenarios to identify hidden vulnerabilities. 
These exercises assess the preparedness of our people, 
systems, and processes. The results offer actionable insights 
to strengthen our security framework and enhance resilience 
against cyber threats and data breaches. 
Cybersecurity Awareness and Training 
A strong focus is placed on cybersecurity and data privacy 
through regular training and awareness programmes for our 
employees and third party contractors. Under the flagship 
Cyber Jagruti programme, mandatory sessions are conduct -ed on IT security controls, prevention of data breaches, and 
responsible handling of Personally Identifiable Information 
(PII). The programme includes periodic LMS-based modules 
for both new joiners and existing employees, along with 
annual refresher sessions to keep knowledge up-to-date. 
To keep our workforce informed and vigilant, we use a 
variety of training formats such as emailers, videos, presen-
tations, and course materials, along with phishing simulations 
to assess awareness and compliance with policies. A dedi-
cated Cyber Jagruti channel on Teams is used to keep staff 
informed about evolving data security and privacy practices. 
In addition, regular cybersecurity communications are shared 
to promote safe practices for both organisational and per -
sonal systems. 
Business Continuity 
Maintaining operational resilience remains paramount to us, 
and we have established a robust business continuity plan 
(BCP) to protect our operations. Our cloud based disaster 
recovery site serves as a safeguard to ensure continuity 
during unforeseen disruptions. In addition, a Cyber Incident 
Response and Recovery process has been established to 
minimise business disruptions arising from cybersecurity 
incidents. 
In line with strengthening data protection and privacy 
practices, we have undertaken targeted initiatives across the 
organisation. Data privacy assessments have been carried 
out for select brands, alongside the development of a DP -
DP-aligned policy and process framework for ABLBL. Data 
leakage prevention technologies have been implemented to 
detect potential exposure of Personally Identifiable Infor -
mation (PII), supported by the onboarding of a group-level 
data privacy platform. Cookie consent mechanisms have 
also been introduced across select brands for international 
users, ensuring compliance with regulations such as GDPR 
and CCPA. Additionally, focused efforts have been initiated 
to minimise PII exposure during data sharing across systems 
and processes. 
Ongoing maintenance, system updates, and semiannual 
testing of business continuity plans are undertaken to assess 
their effectiveness and ensure preparedness to respond to 
contingencies. These proactive efforts enhance operational 
resilience and help minimise the impact of business disrup-
tions, ensuring continuity of business operations. Customer Data privacy 
Our data privacy framework incorporates strong safeguards, 
including data leakage prevention systems, encryption of 
data in transit using Transport Layer Security (TLS), strong 
access controls, and multifactor authentication protocols. 
These controls are supported by ongoing enhancement of 
our systems and processes. Through these efforts, we aim 
to ensure the confidentiality and integrity of customer data, 
protecting it against unauthorised access or misuse. 
In line with our privacy policy, customers are equipped 
with the right to request deletion or correction of their per -
sonal data by contacting the grievance officer via email. In 
alignment with GDPR and CCPA requirements, international 
users visiting our brand websites are presented with a cookie 
consent pop up option, enabling them to choose whether to 
allow or restrict data tracking. 
Incident Response Mechanism 
Adhering to Information Technology Infrastructure Library 
(ITIL) standards, a structured incident management frame-
work has been put in place. Any instance of suspicious 
activity or potential security breach is reported through 
our helpdesk portal and promptly escalated to the relevant 
stakeholders, ensuring timely response and resolution within 
defined Service Level Agreements (SLAs). 
Our escalation framework empowers employees to report 
incidents, vulnerabilities, or suspicious activities swiftly and 
efficiently. This ensures that risks are identified, evaluated, 
and addressed at an early stage, supporting a proactive and 
vigilant security culture across the organisation. An inter -
nal ticketing system is in place for employees to facilitate 
efficient reporting while dedicated and trained personnel 
oversee the investigation of information security incidents 
and conduct detailed root cause analyses to prevent recur -
rence. The findings are reviewed and authorised by respec -
tive business unit IT teams, while critical findings with wider 
implications are escalated for approval by the Chief Digital 
and Information Technology Officer. 
During FY 2025-26, no incidents of data breaches or 
information security lapses were reported.  No substantiated 
complaints related to customer privacy or data protection 
were received, reinforcing the Company’s commitment to 
safeguarding data and maintaining stakeholder trust. INTELLECTUAL CAPITAL

Our Management 
Our dedication to natural capital extends beyond resource 
preservation, it fundamentally reshapes how we operate, 
innovate, and scale. 
Our environmental targets have catalysed a shift in 
mindset, moving from managing footprints to actively regen-
erating ecosystems. Through ReEarth, our flagship sustain-
ability programme, environmental performance has been woven into every layer of the organisation. Our approach 
is anchored in a rigorous policy framework encompassing 
the Environmental Policy , Biodiversity Policy , Sustainabili-
ty Policy , and Sustainable Supply Chain and Procurement 
Policy . We engage with internal and external stakeholders to 
continuously sharpen and execute the Environmental Policy 
alongside initiatives that address pressing environmental 
challenges. 
We have nine facilities certified with ISO 9001, ISO 14001

and ISO 45001. Additionally, our Europa Garment facility 
is certified with ISO 50001. These third-party certification 
underscores our commitment to continual improvement and 
operational excellence. ESG considerations are anchored in 
a structured, multi-tiered framework that provides robust 
oversight, and is also fully embedded within our Enterprise 
Risk Management framework, enabling simultaneous evalua-

decision-making at every level. 
Stringent guidelines have been established to maintain 
alignment with global best practices. Comprehensive ESG 
training equips employees with the awareness to understand 
our environmental impact, identify risks, deploy sustainable 
solutions, and cultivate a culture of responsible, informed 
decision-making. We maintain rigorous regulatory compli-

sanctions were imposed by Central Pollution Control Board 
(CPCB) / State Pollution Control Board (SPCB). There have 
been no instances of violations or non-compliance during 
the reporting year. Beyond regulatory adherence, our robust 
governance mechanism continues to guide us in ensuring 
environmental preservation and long-term stewardship.  
ESG Governance
Our ESG governance framework follows a structured, 
multi-layered approach that ensures robust oversight of  
climate and ESG related risks while promoting transparency 
and ethical decision making.
At the highest level, the Board of Directors provides 
strategic oversight by approving sustainability policies and 
guiding senior management on ESG initiatives. Semi-annual 
Board meetings focus on climate-related risks and opportu-nities, strategies, policies, and overall performance to ensure 
alignment with long-term sustainability objectives. The 
Board-level Risk Management and Sustainability Committee 
(RMSC) plays a key role in monitoring and addressing ESG 
matters, including climate and ESG related issues. Meeting 
bi-annually, the Committee reviews progress and reports 
updates to the Board. In addition, the Board of Directors, 
including RMSC members, regularly participates in capaci-
ty-building sessions on emerging ESG developments.
Leadership engagement is central to advancing our 
company’s sustainability agenda. The Managing Director de-
fines the overall strategic direction, while the Chief Sustain-
ability Officer (CSO) leads the development and execution 
of sustainability and climate strategies. The CSO conducts 
quarterly reviews to monitor progress in implementing CSR 
and sustainability initiatives. Budget allocations for CSR and 
sustainability programmes are strategically planned and 
approved to ensure alignment with business objectives, with 
oversight and guidance from the RMSC and the Corporate 
Social Responsibility Committee (CSRC).
Furthermore, a Management Committee consisting of 
CXOs and senior management enabling has been set up 
to ensure effective communication and cooperation across 
departments, leading to the seamless integration of ESG 
principles into business operations. At the operational level, 
implementation teams conduct bi-monthly discussions with 
business unit heads to address ESG and climate related con-
cerns across factories, warehouses, and retail outlets. These 
regular interactions ensure that employees remain actively 
involved and empowered to contribute to sustainability 
initiatives, strengthening a culture of responsibility across the 
organisation. 
Financial incentives play a pivotal role in driving sustain-ability performance and ensuring alignment with climate and 
sustainability targets. ESG KPIs are integrated into the vari-
able remuneration of the Management Committee, including 
CEOs, the CSO, and other CXOs. These performance-linked 
incentives extend to functional heads and sustainability team 
members.
 
Climate Strategy
 
At ABLBL, we recognise the industry’s influence on climate 
change, and actively work to mitigate the environmental im-
pact of our operations and products. Climate considerations 
are integral to financial, strategic, and operational decisions, 
ensuring a responsible approach to sustainability. 
Our near-term emission reduction targets, validated 
by the Science Based Targets Initiative (SBTi), reflect an 
unwavering commitment to climate action. We are targeting 
a 54.6% absolute reduction in Scope 1 and 2 emissions by FY 
2032-33 against the FY 2022-23 baseline, alongside a 32.5% 
absolute reduction in Scope 3 emissions across purchased 
goods and services, fuel and energy-related activities, and 
franchises within the same timeframe. We are also aligned 
with the Aditya Birla Group’s decarbonisation strategy, 
pursuing net zero carbon emissions by 2050 through energy 
efficiency programmes, low carbon growth, product stew -
ardship, and carbon sequestration projects. Periodic climate 
change risk assessments are conducted in accordance with 
the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures 
(TCFD) to evaluate climate-related challenges across all 
operational sites including existing manufacturing facilities, 
warehouses, and retail stores, as well as upstream and down-
stream activities.Climate risks are assessed against current and anticipat -
ed regulations, technological shifts, legal exposure, market 
dynamics, reputational considerations, and both acute and 
chronic physical risks. These risks and opportunities are 
further incorporated in our enterprise risk management 
framework. Risk evaluation spans three distinct timeframes: 
short-term (up to 2030), medium-term (2030–2040), and 
long-term (beyond 2040). Scenario analyses leverage the 
Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) Repre-
sentation Concentration Pathways (RCP 2.6, RCP 4.5, RCP 6, 
and RCP 8.5) and Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSP1-1.9, 
SSP1- 2.6, SSP2-4.5, SSP3-7.0, SSP5-8.5) to assess potential 
physical risks, including temperature and precipitation fluc -
tuations across operational sites. Additionally, transition risks 
are analysed using scenarios from the International Energy 
Agency (IEA), including the Net Zero Emissions by 2050 
Scenario (NZE), the Announced Pledges Scenario (APS), 
the Stated Policies Scenario (STEPS), and the Sustainable 
Development Scenario (SDS). These insights, derived from 
both quantitative and qualitative models, help identify 
climate risks, develop mitigation strategies, and capitalise on 
emerging opportunities. To build resilience against identified 
risks, comprehensive, context-specific plans have been devel-
oped covering 100% of operations including all new facilities, 
with adaptation measures prioritised for implementation 
within five years, ensuring the organisation remains agile and 
well-prepared to navigate climate-related challenges.
We have established a transition plan to align with global 
net-zero GHG emission goals, with a clear commitment to 
supporting the Paris Agreement objective of limiting global 
warming to 1.5°C. Our approach includes defined decarboni-
sation levers and planned actions to drive progress towards 
our emission reduction targets. We actively engage with key 
stakeholders, including our value chain partners and indus-
try associations, to gather inputs and support the effective 
implementation of our transition pathway. Through these 
efforts, we aim to progressively advance our climate strategy 
and strengthen alignment with global climate commitments.

Fashion and Retail Limited (ABFRL) and Aditya Birla Lifestyle

targets were validated by the Science Based Targets initia-
tive (SBTi) in 2024, the demerger necessitated a review of 
the Company’s greenhouse gas (GHG) inventory and target 
applicability in accordance with the SBTi Corporate Net-Zero 
and Near-Term Criteria.
Consistent with SBTi requirements, ABFRL sought formal 
guidance on the implications of the demerger for its validat -
ed targets and base year emissions inventory. SBTi guid-
ance specifies that companies must recalculate their base 
year emissions where structural changes, such as mergers, 
acquisitions, divestments, or demergers; result in a material 
change to the emissions inventory. Such recalculations are 
intended to preserve consistency, transparency, and compa-
rability of progress against established targets.
SBTi further clarified that a recalculation of base year 
emissions does not automatically trigger target revalidation. 
Existing validated targets may continue to remain valid, 
provided that the recalculated inventory does not materially 
alter the ambition level, organisational boundary, target cov -
erage, or methodological alignment of the original commit -
ment. Revalidation is generally required only where structural 
change significantly affects the integrity or ambition of the 
approved target pathway.
Accordingly, ABFRL undertook a detailed assessment 
internally, to evaluate the impact of the demerger on its sci-
ence-based targets. The assessment concluded that although 
the demerger constitutes a material structural change requir -
ing recalculation of base year emissions, it does not affect 
the underlying ambition, target methodology, or coverage 
requirements of the existing SBTi-approved targets.
Following the recalculation exercise, both ABFRL and ABLBL 
continue to satisfy the minimum target-boundary coverage 
thresholds prescribed by SBTi:
• Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions coverage exceeds 95% of 
total emissions; and
• Scope 3 emissions coverage exceeds 67%.
As both entities continue to meet the applicable SBTi 
coverage requirements and the ambition of the validated 
targets remains unchanged, revalidation or resubmission of 
targets to SBTi is not required at this stage. The principal 
action arising from the demerger is the recalculation and 
restatement of base year emissions to reflect the revised 
organisational boundaries of ABFRL and ABLBL.RECALCULATED FY 2023 BASE YEAR EMISSIONS

Energy Management
At ABLBL, we are committed to optimising energy consump-
tion and enhancing efficiency through targeted initiatives. 
Energy consumption data is systematically captured through 
the ReEarth portal. Energy sources include grid electricity, 
diesel, and renewable energy comprising solar and biomass. All reported data is subject to independent third-party assur -
ance to ensure accuracy, reliability, and transparency. We do 
not have any energy consumption outside our organisational 
boundaries.
We conduct regular employee awareness sessions on en-
ergy conservation to promote responsible energy use across 
our operations. Periodic energy audits enable us to identify 
improvement opportunities and ensure systematic monitor -
ing of progress. Our strong commitment to energy efficiency 
is further demonstrated by the ISO 50001 Energy Manage-
ment Systems certification awarded to our Europa Garments 
facility. To diversify our energy mix, we have integrated solar 
rooftops and solar streetlights across facilities alongside 
transition to biomass-based briquettes as boiler fuel. We 
strengthened on-site solar generation at the Haritha Appar -
els facility as part of our renewable energy roadmap while 
development programmes towards a 100% renewable energy 
setup have also been initiated.  Real-time monitoring of 
solar generation at nine facilities allows for optimal capacity 
utilisation, while also maximising solar generation efficiency. 
In FY 2025-26, our solar energy consumption reached 30.28 
lakhs units, reinforcing our commitment to green energy 
solutions. We invest in renewable energy credits to offset 
emissions, supporting a more responsible and sustainable 
approach to energy management. Through these combined efforts, we continue to drive meaningful reductions in our 
environmental footprint while advancing the transition to 
cleaner energy alternatives. The increase in renewable ener -
gy consumption is due to the installation of rooftop solar at 
a few of our facilities. Furthermore, we are accelerating the 
shift to renewable energy, targeting 80% renewable sourcing 
across owned operations by 2030 and Net Zero by 2050 in 
alignment with the ABG commitment. We aim to reduce our 
energy consumption and continuously assess our progress to 
ensure effective energy management.  
Energy Conservation Initiatives
 
We have implemented multiple energy conservation initia-
tives, including the installation of energy-efficient lighting 
systems such as LED lights integrated with motion sensors, 
deployment of rooftop solar panels and solar streetlights, 
and the adoption of robust operations and maintenance 
(O&M) best practices across our electrical systems. To further 
reduce energy consumption, we are progressively shifting 
towards renewable energy sources and increasing the use 
of biomass-based boilers. Through these initiatives we have 
been able to reduce our energy intensity over the years as 
well as were able to maintain our product energy intensity 
over the past three years.

racy.  Additionally, a location-based methodology has been 
adopted for the assessment of Scope 2 emissions.

strengthened energy monitoring and equipment tracking ,

Raising awareness on responsible water usage is a key focus,

Conservation Initiatives 
 
We have implemented a range of water conservation mea-
sures across our operations, including the installation of 
low-water fixtures such as aerators, adoption of rainwater 
harvesting systems and artificial aquifer recharge, and the 
installation of sewage treatment plants. Treated water is 
recycled and reused for flushing and gardening purposes, 
supported by the deployment of remote water monitoring 
systems. To further enhance operational efficiency, we have 
implemented advanced IoT- and cloud-based solutions 
that provide real-time insights to optimise water usage 
and reduce consumption. These efforts are complemented 
by water-efficient fixtures, artificial recharge systems, and 
automated treatment technologies, enabling us to minimise 
water wastage and strengthen overall water management 
performance.
Water Discharge
We maintain Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) at all our facilities. 
Furthermore, we have equipped all our facilities with sewage 
treatment plants (STPs) to enhance wastewater quality and enable effective recycling. To ensure full compliance, 
we do regular testing of physical, chemical, and biological 
parameters. The treated water from these STPs is reused for 
gardening and flushing purposes, in compliance with applica-
ble regulatory norms. Water quality is rigorously monitored 
in compliance with state pollution control guidelines, with 
adherence maintained across all national, regional, and local 
air and water consent requirements. These initiatives help 
us minimise freshwater withdrawals, mitigate pollution risks, 
and reinforce our commitment to sustainable water manage-
ment.  During the reporting period, we successfully recycled 
72% of the water withdrawn, adhering to the Aditya Birla 
Group’s technical standard on wastewater management.
 
Managing Water-Stressed Areas
We annually assess water risks using the WRI Aqueduct 
tool, examining availability, demand, and future projections 
to maneuver through conservation efforts. Our assessment 
indicates that our facilities and warehouses in Bengaluru fall 
within water-stressed locations. To limit freshwater reliance 
in these areas, we implement enhanced recycling systems, 
rainwater harvesting, and water-efficient technologies, sup-
porting our commitment to responsible water management 
and sustainability. Our integrated approach ensures we use 
water judiciously while returning more than we consume.

Waste Management  
Strategic waste management is vital for reducing environ-
mental impact, conserving resources, and enhancing oper -
ational sustainability. We have implemented defined guide-
lines and Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for various 
waste types to ensure effective segregation, safe handling 
and compliant disposal, supporting sustainable waste man-agement across operations. We adopt a circular approach to 
waste management by systematically segregating, recycling, 
and reusing waste, thereby reducing our reliance on virgin re-
sources. This approach contributes to lower water and ener -
gy consumption and minimises environmental impact across 
our production cycle. We are committed to minimising waste 
generation and diverting it from landfills, with the objective 
of transforming waste into a resource for new products and 
closing the loop within our operations.
Our waste management approach involves close col-
laboration between internal teams, operations teams, and 
authorised vendors to ensure effective handling, monitor -
ing, and disposal of waste across our facilities. Our facilities 
ensure proper segregation and maintain detailed records. Trained personnel verify data accuracy and en-
sure compliance with environmental regulations, 
while authorised vendors support responsible 
disposal practices aligned with our zero waste to 
landfill ambition. Cross-functional collaboration 
across departments enables thorough validation 
of data completeness and accuracy. This integrat -
ed system supports effective waste governance, 
minimises environmental impact, and strength-
ens our progress toward sustainability goals. We 
have established a dedicated waste management 
task force responsible for waste reduction, seg-
regation, safe handling, and collection. The team 
ensures appropriate disposal through recycling, 
reuse, composting via authorised vendors, and 
in-house methods.
Investment in innovative technologies has 
played a pivotal role in reducing waste. Employ -
ee training is equally important to our waste 
management approach. Awareness programmes 
are conducted to educate staff on effective waste 
reduction techniques, reinforcing responsible 
practices that support long-term sustainability. 
These holistic waste reduction strategies, includ-
ing the Reduce-Reuse-Recycle approach, waste 
diversion from landfills, recycling, co-processing, 
and composting systems have led to our achieve-
ment of the third-party certified “Zero Waste to 
Landfill” certification in July 2022, recognised by 
both USGBC True Zero Gold and Bureau Veritas. 
These certifications affirm our commitment to 
circularity and sustainable resource management.  
 We have a robust waste management system comprises 
routine audits and periodic monitoring of waste dispos-
al systems, which helps confirm safe handling practices, 
accurately quantify waste sent to authorised recyclers, and 
identify areas for improvement. Biomedical and sanitary 
waste undergo incineration, ensuring safe treatment, while 
non-hazardous waste is either recycled or repurposed. Food 
waste is composted using in-house biodigesters, converting 
it into bio-manure for farming. All disposal processes comply 
with operating regulatory requirements, and we carefully se-
lect waste disposal facilities and recyclers through stringent 
due diligence to prevent contamination during the disposal 
process. WASTE GENERATION (MT)

Waste Management Initiatives 
We are striving to achieve zero waste to landfill across our 
facilities, offices, and warehouses, with pilot programmes 
extended to select retail stores. Our approach focuses on 
diverting waste from landfills, ensuring that waste undergoes 
appropriate recycling processes, and preventing contamina-
tion across the waste management lifecycle.
Key initiatives include the transition to sustainable packaging by replacing plastics and adopting reusable crates 
for the transportation of finished goods. Additionally, we 
leverage optimised, digitised tools for garment marking and 
cutting, which has significantly reduced waste generation in 
our manufacturing processes.
Packaging Management 
We continuously strive to strengthen our systems and 
processes and, as a leader in the apparel retail sector, have 
committed to using 100% sustainable packaging material by 
2030. Our packaging strategy focuses on design optimisa-
tion, reduction and recycling; to reduce pollutant content.

Raw Material Management 
Responsible sourcing of raw materials is fundamental to mi-
nimising environmental impact and sustaining ethical supply 
chains within the apparel retail sector. We are committed to increasing the use of sustainable materials, supported by 
strong standards of social responsibility and environmental 
stewardship.
We have developed an internal framework for sustain-
able attributes that encompasses sustainable raw materials, 
production processes, manufacturing facilities, packaging, 
and sustainable livelihoods. A consolidated target has been 
established for the proportion of sustainable and recycled 
raw materials, with performance monitored and reported on 
both a half-yearly and annual basis. In FY 2025-26, 93% of 
our products had at least one sustainable attribute. By 2030, 
we aim to incorporate at least one sustainable attribute 
across 100% of our garments, by volume.
As part of this commitment, we source high-quality raw 
materials with a focus on minimising environmental and 
social impacts across the value chain. Guided by recognised 
tools and standards, we prioritise the use of responsibly 
sourced and lower-impact materials, including BCI Cotton, 
Liva Eco, FSC-certified Birla Modal, and recycled fibres, while 
maintaining high standards of quality, performance, and 
ethical manufacturing. We also drive sustainable product in-
novation through initiatives such as Van Heusen’s Move Labs

incorporate eco-friendly materials and resource-efficient 
production processes. To support continuous improvement, 
we use a cradle-to-grave Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) ap-
proach to evaluate environmental and social impacts, identify 
opportunities for greater resource efficiency, and strengthen

We have internally identified cotton as a priority raw ma-

methods and promoting responsible cotton sourcing such as

Product Sustainability 
We integrate sustainability into product design by prioritising 
responsibly sourced fabrics, recycled fibres, and biodegrad-
able materials. Our optimised production processes reduce 
waste while improving product durability and recyclability.
To evaluate environmental impact, we conduct compre-
hensive Lifecycle Assessments (LCA) from cradle to grave, 
analysing energy consumption, GHG emissions, water usage, 
and waste generation. These assessments help identify key 
hotspots, including Scope 3 emissions, and guide innovation 
in sustainable product development.
We have identified ten key impact categories and con-
tinuously refine our practices to lower our environmental 
footprint while meeting rising consumer expectations for 
sustainability. LCA studies have been completed for casual 
and formal shirts, T-shirts, and denim jeans, covering 40% of our turnover, along with a defined set of associated risks and 
mitigation measures.
 
Biodiversity Management 
Biodiversity plays an important role in sustaining apparel 
manufacturing under fashion industry by ensuring the avail-
ability of key natural raw materials such as cotton, wool, and 
leather, while maintaining ecological balance across sourcing 
and production ecosystems.
At ABLBL, biodiversity considerations are integrated 
across our apparel manufacturing operations, from raw ma-
terial sourcing to factory-level processes. 
Guided by our Biodiversity Policy and the Aditya Birla 
Group’s biodiversity management framework, aligned with 
the Convention on Biological Diversity—we adopt a structured 
and proactive approach to managing biodiversity impacts. 
We recognise that apparel manufacturing has upstream and 
operational dependencies on biodiversity, hence we are com-
mitted to minimising our impact on ecosystems by avoiding 
operations in ecologically sensitive areas and integrating 
biodiversity considerations into our overall business strategy.
Our Approach to Biodiversity Conservation
To systematically manage biodiversity-related risks and 
opportunities, we have developed a Biodiversity Roadmap 
based on the LEAP framework. This roadmap enables us 
to identify, assess, and respond to biodiversity challenges 
across our operations. 
This plan enables us to identify, assess, and address biodiversity challenges across our textile manufacturing op-
erations. Going forward, we will evaluate our dependence on 
key raw materials such as cotton, fibres, and chemicals, while 
assessing our impact on land use change, climate change, 
resource extraction, and pollution.
These insights will guide targeted conservation and mitiga-
tion efforts across our facilities, surrounding ecosystems, and 
throughout our supply chain, including tier 1 and tier 2 suppli-
ers. Our roadmap is structured around short-, medium-, and 
long-term goals, ensuring continuous progress in strengthen-
ing biodiversity management within our value chain.
Biodiversity Assessment & Mitigation
We undertook an initial biodiversity assessment using the 
Integrated Biodiversity Assessment Tool (IBAT), an elaborate 
framework which enables the identification of key biodi-
versity areas surrounding our operations and species from 
the IUCN Red List. The findings provide the base for our 
biodiversity management plan, aligned with the Convention 
on Biological Diversity and guided by the LEAP approach. 
The assessment was undertaken using a location specific 
approach across 11 manufacturing facilities, 2 offices, and 
3 warehouses. IBAT drew on multiple databases, including 
the IUCN Red List of Threatened Species and the Threats 
Classification Scheme, to generate the results. Our biodiver -
sity strategy is also designed to align with the Task Force on 
Nature-related Financial Disclosures (TNFD) requirements.
We assess the biodiversity and ecosystem service risks 
associated with existing and planned activities to support 
informed planning and execution. And the potential impacts 
are managed through the mitigation hierarchy, prioritising 
avoidance and minimisation, followed by restoration, and 
offsetting residual impacts where required.
Biodiversity Conservation Initiatives 
Our mitigation efforts include plantation initiatives to restore 
green spaces and enhance biodiversity. At the Van Heusen 
Innerwear warehouse in Bangalore, a Miyawaki forest has 
been developed to accelerate growth and improve soil health 
through mixed-species planting. We also carry out affor -
estation and reforestation drives across operational sites, 
planting native species to support ecosystems, facilitating 
better air quality and sequester carbon.
Through these initiatives, biodiversity is systematically embedded into our manufacturing strategy, enabling respon-
sible production while protecting the natural ecosystems that 
support long-term business resilience.
Sustainable Infrastructure
At ABLBL, we focus on creating sustainable infrastructure by 
aligning our facilities with globally recognised green building 
standards, enabling us to reduce environmental impact while 
improving operational performance. Five of our facilities are 
certified by the Indian Green Building Council (IGBC) and the 
US Green Building Council (USGBC), reflecting our adoption 
of eco friendly materials, efficient technologies, and sustain-
able design practices.

Green Retail at Aditya Birla
The Green Retail for Aditya Birla (GRAB) initiative is aimed 
at assessing, monitoring, and enhancing the sustainability 
performance of retail stores, in alignment with our sustain-
ability commitments and the Science-Based Targets initiative 
(SBTi). The GRAB Store Checklist incorporates national and 
international green building standards such as LEED and 
IGBC, while being adapted to regional and industry-specific 
practices. Covering both environmental and safety param-
eters, it facilitates comprehensive evaluations by internal 
teams.
Stores are evaluated against GRAB standards through 
a structured scoring system that recognises sustainability 
efforts and provides benchmarks for improvement. The 
ratings track progress and highlight areas for further 
development, ensuring the continuous refinement of 
sustainability initiatives. During FY 2025-26, 34 stores of 
ABLBL went through GRAB Assessment.

a priority, enabling better control and overall reduction in 
usage. We also strive to implement smart lighting solutions, 
including occupancy sensor-based systems for non-occupied 
areas, to minimise unnecessary energy expenditure.
Expanding the adoption of renewable energy remains 
central to our vision, with an increased focus on solar energy 
integration. We seek to enhance water conservation by in-

reuse of treated water. Our efforts will also extend to sustain-
able branding and packaging, as we work towards using fully 
recycled material carry bags, eliminating single-use plastic 
bottles, and expanding the take-back programme. Addi-
tionally, we aim to further refine cooling systems to improve 
efficiency and reduce overall energy consumption.
These advancements will drive continued progress 
towards achieving our sustainability objectives and reinforce 
responsible retail practices.

Tailoring Impact for Communities
As a responsible organisation, we are conscious of the 
impact our actions have on the society and environment 
around us. We firmly believe that embedding social respon-
sibility within our operations enables us to create meaningful 
and lasting value for the communities we serve. Through our 
Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) initiatives, we focus on 
driving inclusive development and addressing key societal 
needs. Our interventions are thoughtfully designed to create 
a positive and tangible difference in the lives of community 
members, reflecting our commitment to responsible and 
sustainable growth.
                                                                                                           
Our CSR Approach
We follow the Aditya Birla Group’s Corporate Social Respon-
sibility (CSR) Policy which aims at reaching out to under -
served communities and a firm conviction in the Trusteeship 
concept, which entails transcending business interests and 
working towards making a meaningful difference to those 
communities. We undertake CSR interventions in Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Odisha and Andhra Pradesh through Aditya Birla 
Fashion and Retail Jan Kalyan Trust (ABFR-JKT). 
The Aditya Birla Centre for Community Initiatives and Rural 
Development provides the vision under the leadership of its 
Chairperson, Mrs. Rajashree Birla. The Centre provides stra-
tegic direction and thrust areas for our work, while ensuring 
effective performance management. This vision underlines 
all CSR activities. We have an exclusive CSR team that also 
receives guidance from Dr. Pragnya Ram, the Group Executive 
President - CSR, Legacy Documentation & Archive, who guides 
and ensures systematic implementation of its CSR initiatives. 
Our continuous focus is to create sustainable and impact -
ful CSR programmes that are aligned to the Group’s CSR Vi-
sion. Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail Jan Kalyan Trust focuses 
its CSR initiatives under five pillars i.e. Education, Health & 
Sanitation, Sustainable Livelihood, Water & Watershed and 
Digitalization. These pillars are the guiding thematic areas 
for the projects. The projects, 1) Village Development Project, 
Karnataka and Tamil Nadu, 2) Village Development Project, 
Odisha and 3) Village Development Project, Andhra Pradesh.
We strongly encourage voluntary employee participation 
in the CSR activities and has a policy in place to facilitate em-ployee volunteering.

CSR Policy and Governance
Our Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) Policy is anchored 
in our commitment to contribute meaningfully to the social 
and economic development of the communities in which we 
operate. In line with the provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 and guided by the Aditya Birla Group’s philosophy of 
trusteeship, we go beyond business objectives to address 
the quality-of-life challenges faced by underserved commu-
nities. Through a structured and disciplined approach, our 
policy outlines the framework for planning, implementation 
and monitoring of CSR initiatives, ensuring alignment with 
national priorities and the United Nations Sustainable Devel-
opment Goals. We remain committed to creating sustainable 
and inclusive impact while upholding the highest standards 
of responsibility and governance.
Furthermore, our steadfast CSR governance underpins 
effective implementation of our initiatives.
